# How desflow Works

This page shows how desflow is built: the parts that run a model, why each one exists, and how a run moves through them. Each part links to the How It Works section that describes it in full.

One run moves through the parts of desflow like this:

Whichever way a model is written, it builds one environment, and one run goes the same way from there. The registry paths, the [records](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md), the batching and the connectors are therefore the same in all three ways. [How It Works](#how-it-works) follows a model from its file or script to the environment.

______________________________________________________________________

## What It Is

desflow is built on [SimPy](https://simpy.readthedocs.io/). SimPy gives the event list, the clock, processes and resources, and desflow keeps all of them. SimPy leaves seven things to the modeller, and each part of desflow adds one of them:

| Left to the modeller in SimPy                                                                       | What desflow adds                                                                      | Read                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| the code around a model: a class of parameters, an entity class, a model class and a loop over runs | three ways to write a model, each built on the one below                               | [Writing a Model](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/index.md)                               |
| one pacing `factor`, fixed when the environment is made                                             | one environment that runs history at full speed, then switches to the wall clock       | [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#how-it-works)                          |
| random times, drawn by the model's own code                                                         | ten checked distributions, each with a random stream of its own                        | [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/#how-it-works)  |
| parameters that only the model's code changes                                                       | a registry of named paths that connectors, scenarios and processes change during a run | [Live Parameters](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#how-it-works) |
| resources, stores and containers that keep the capacity they were made with                         | resources, stores and containers whose capacity follows the registry                   | [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#how-it-works)                                      |
| output, which the model prints or logs                                                              | records of a fixed shape, written to sinks on a thread of their own                    | [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#how-it-works)                   |
| statistics, replications and confidence intervals                                                   | statistics collected during the run, replications, experiments and `explain`           | [Built-in Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#how-it-works)                   |

[Coming from SimPy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/coming-from-simpy/#what-desflow-changes) compares each change with plain SimPy.

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

Look first at how a model gets from a file or a script to a run, then at the parts the run holds:

Each of the three ways ends in one `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. A YAML file is read by `blueprint`: `loader` reads the file, including `!python` and `!include`, `models` define and check each section, and `build` turns the sections into calls on `SimulationContext`; the arrow labelled calls the builder shows them. A builder script makes those calls itself, with the builder's methods and decorators. A low-level script makes neither: it builds the environment by hand and writes SimPy processes against it. [Writing a Model](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/index.md) helps choose between them.

`SimulationContext` in `builder.context` collects what a model declares. `run()` checks the declarations and builds the environment, then starts the model's loops and processes and runs it, in the order [What `run()` Does](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#what-run-does) lists. The environment holds the parts in the row under it:

- **registry:** holds every live parameter ([Live Parameters](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#how-it-works)).
- **statistics:** collects the measures of the run while it goes on ([Built-in Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#how-it-works)).
- **egress queue:** the records that tasks and processes publish are buffered for each sink, and full batches wait in a queue. `connectors/egress` writes from it, on a thread of its own, and the arrow points the way the records go ([Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#how-it-works)).
- **connectors/ingress:** read parameter changes from outside, on a thread of their own, and update the registry. The arrow points up, because a change reaches the model only through the registry; the environment applies each one from a queue ([Ingress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/ingress/#how-it-works)). [Threads and Queues](#threads-and-queues) shows both queues.

The group at the bottom holds the tools. `cli` is the `desflow` command and calls `loading`, the path by which `desflow run` and `desflow explain` turn a blueprint or a builder file into a context ([Command Line](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/#how-it-works)). `analysis` runs a model many times for [replications](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/replications/#how-it-works) and [experiments](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/experiments/#how-it-works). `cli` and `explain` read a blueprint or a builder file; `analysis` also runs a low-level model, as a `LowLevelModel`, from Python. `explain` is in the last row of the table below.

Each part is described in full on its own page. In short:

| Part                             | How it works                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Read                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Writing a model                  | A YAML blueprint, the builder and the low-level API are layers. `from_yaml` makes the calls a builder script makes, and the builder's `run()` makes the calls a low-level script writes by hand.                            | [YAML Blueprints](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#how-it-works), [What `run()` Does](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#what-run-does)                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Environment and pacing           | `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` is SimPy's `RealtimeEnvironment` with the registry, the connectors and the statistics added. It runs without waiting at `factor: 0` and switches to real time at `go_live_at`.                 | [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/#how-it-works)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Random times                     | A distribution reads its parameters at each draw, so a change applies from the next draw. Each one has its own random stream, made from the run's seed and its registry path.                                               | [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/#how-it-works)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Registry                         | Every live value sits under a dot path, such as `Shop.service.packing.mean`. Each update is checked before it is stored.                                                                                                    | [Live Parameters](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#how-it-works)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Resources, stores and containers | Each waits on its registry path, so its capacity changes during a run. A resource that shrinks lets its busy units finish.                                                                                                  | [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#how-it-works), [Stores and Containers](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/stores-and-containers/#how-it-works)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Threads, ingress and egress      | The SimPy thread runs the model. Ingress and egress run their connectors on threads of their own, each on an asyncio loop, so a network wait never stalls a simulation step.                                                | [Threads and Queues](#threads-and-queues), which also compares these queues with the waiting lines of the model; [Ingress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/ingress/#how-it-works), [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#how-it-works), [Write a Connector](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/write-a-connector/index.md) |
| Measurement and explain          | One statistics object collects readings while the run goes on. Replications run the model again for each seed and give a Student t interval. `desflow explain` applies queueing formulas to the model before anything runs. | [Built-in Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#how-it-works), [Replications](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/replications/#how-it-works), [Experiments](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/experiments/#how-it-works), [Command Line](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/#how-it-works)                                                                |

### How a YAML File Becomes Builder Calls

Follow the file down the left column, then look at the group on the right, which joins each section of the file to the builder call it becomes:

- **loader** reads the file, replaces `${VAR}` with an environment variable, and resolves `!python` and `!include` ([YAML Blueprints](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#how-it-works)). It keeps the line each key came from, so an error names the line.
- **models** checks each section and refuses an unknown key, so a misspelt key is reported, not ignored.
- **build** makes one builder call for each entry, so a YAML file and a builder script that make the same calls build the same model. From `SimulationContext` on, a run goes as the next diagram shows.

### How a Builder Script Becomes a Run

Look at the two halves: the top shows where the builder keeps what a script declares, and the group below shows what `run()` does with it, in order. `run()` is `start()`, which makes steps 1 to 4, then `finish()`, which makes step 5; a script that steps through a run itself calls `start()` alone:

1. **checks:** every name a declaration refers to is checked first, and a wrong model is refused with a `ValueError` before anything is built.
1. **keeps the run:** each `start()` makes a new run state, so a second run never starts from what the first left.
1. **builds:** the builder makes the parts a low-level script makes by hand, which the next diagram shows: the environment, its registry and statistics, the connectors and the resources.
1. **starts:** the arrival loops and the scenario run as SimPy processes. Each arrival starts a task instance, `TaskRun` runs it, and `flow` routes its entity to the next task. A task with a `batch` keeps its place in the batch in `batches`. [What `run()` Does](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#what-run-does) lists these steps.
1. **runs:** the model runs to its `until`, its `stop` or the end of its drain, and the run closes: the last statistics are published and the connectors stop.

### What a Low-Level Script Uses

A low-level script uses the engine directly. Look at the top row for what the script calls, and at the row below it for what the environment holds:

- **environment:** the script creates it, registers its parameters, calls `setup_stats`, `setup_ingress` and `setup_egress`, starts its processes with `env.process`, and calls `run()`.
- **sampler:** draws every random time, with one random stream for each distribution ([Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/#how-it-works)).
- **DynamicResource:** a resource whose capacity follows its registry path ([Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/#how-it-works)).
- **rules:** the checks a blueprint and the builder share; the registry uses one of them to check a capacity before it stores it.
- **expressions, families and replay** serve the builder and YAML: conditions and amounts, resources and signals made from a computed key, and arrivals read from a recorded file.

[ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v1.0.0rc3/ARCHITECTURE.md) draws the same three diagrams as text, with every module.

______________________________________________________________________

## Threads and Queues

### What the Environment Holds

A `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` is SimPy's `RealtimeEnvironment` with four additions: the registry at `env.registry`, the ingress connectors, the egress connectors with their buffers, and the statistics at `env.stats`. Whichever way a model is written, `SimulationContext.run()` builds this environment.

### Threads

A run uses three threads, with queues between them. Records flow from the processes to the sinks, and parameter changes flow from the sources to the registry:

- **SimPy thread:** runs the model. When a process publishes a record, the record goes into a buffer for each sink, and a full buffer is handed to that sink's queue.
- **Egress thread:** runs the sinks' asyncio code, which drains the queues and writes to Kafka, files or databases, so network waits never stall a simulation step.
- **Ingress thread:** runs the sources, which put `(path, value)` pairs on a queue.

### Two Kinds of Queue

The word queue means two different things in desflow:

- **A waiting line in the model** holds entities, such as orders waiting for a packer. A resource keeps its line in `queue`, ordered `fifo`, `lifo` or by `priority`, and a request past its `queue_limit` raises `QueueFull`. Stores and containers have lines of puts and gets that wait. These lines are what a study measures: their lengths and waits are in the records and the statistics.
- **A hand-off queue** holds data on its way between the threads above. The ingress queue has no limit, and the ingress monitor applies it. Each sink has its own queue of at most `max_queued_batches` batches. When a sink's queue is full, the simulation waits, so a slow sink slows the run instead of building a backlog. When it stays full for `drain_stall_seconds`, the run stops rather than lose records. These queues change how fast the records arrive, never what they hold.

### Processes the Environment Starts

Besides your own processes, the environment starts these, as events of its own that `step()` and `peek()` do not count:

- an ingress monitor, which applies queued changes every 0.1 simulation seconds;
- a lag monitor, which publishes `system.simulation.lag_seconds` every `lag_interval`, at a `factor` above 0 or after going live;
- a timed flush per sink, at a `factor` above 0;
- the statistics timer;
- the warm-up reset.

They share SimPy's one event queue with the model's events, so `run()` processes them in order with the model's events. A script that steps the model never sees them. `advance()` and `finish()` run them in the same way. An environment subclass that overrides `step()` sees every event inside `run()`, desflow's own included, and only the model's events when a script steps outside `run()`.

### SimPy and desflow

SimPy's `RealtimeEnvironment` takes one `factor` for the whole run, and raises an error when the model falls behind the wall clock. desflow runs without waiting at `factor: 0`, switches to real time at `go_live_at`, and stamps every record with a logical time. A paced run is strict by default, as SimPy's is, and `strict: false` reports falling behind as telemetry instead. [SimPy and desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/index.md) compares the two.

______________________________________________________________________

## For Contributors

A contributor who changes desflow itself can read [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v1.0.0rc3/ARCHITECTURE.md), which holds the code map and the rules for imports.

# Writing a Model

desflow has three ways to write a simulation: a YAML blueprint, the builder API and the low-level API. This page says how they relate and which to choose. If you are new to desflow, start with [First Simulation](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/first-model/first-simulation/index.md), which shows the same model in all three APIs side by side. Return here to look up a specific component.

______________________________________________________________________

## What It Is

The three are layers, not alternatives. Each layer writes the one below it for you:

- **YAML blueprint:** a file. `SimulationContext.from_yaml`, which `desflow run` calls, reads it and makes the same builder calls a Python script would make, so the result is an ordinary `SimulationContext`.
- **Builder API:** `SimulationContext` collects resources, distributions, tasks and connectors through its methods and decorators. Its `run()` compiles them into a `SimParameter`, builds the environment, registers the parameters and starts the processes.
- **Low-level API:** you write that last step by hand: a `SimParameter`, a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment` that registers it, and SimPy processes that use the environment's resources and publish records.

Because each layer ends in the one below, the layers mix: a blueprint can reference Python written for the builder with `!python`, and a builder process can use the environment directly.

______________________________________________________________________

## How to Use It

|                          | YAML Blueprint                                                                                           | Builder API                                                                                            | Low-level API                                                        |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Entry point**          | `desflow run` or `SimulationContext.from_yaml`                                                           | `SimulationContext`                                                                                    | `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`                                         |
| **What you write**       | the simulation, declared in a file; Python only for logic YAML cannot express, referenced with `!python` | what the system looks like, with decorators for each task's steps                                      | how every event and resource operates, step by step                  |
| **What it does for you** | everything the builder does, and no Python to run                                                        | publishing each task's events, requesting resources, sampling times, routing between tasks, statistics | nothing: you queue, start, time out and release yourself             |
| **Typical use**          | changing rates, capacities, connectors and timed experiments between runs without editing code           | models whose logic is most of the program, and configuration built in code, for example from a loop    | what the builder does not do, such as resources created during a run |

### Which to Choose

- **YAML blueprint** when the configuration is what changes between runs: a new arrival rate, another packer, a different broker, a scripted experiment. A file is easy to review and to diff, a run is one command, and a blueprint has a scenario of timed changes on the simulation clock built in. Logic that YAML cannot express goes in a Python module beside the file, as [Call Python from YAML](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/yaml-advanced/index.md) shows.
- **Builder API** when most of the program is logic and you want it in one Python file, or when you build the configuration in code.
- **Low-level API** when you need what the builder does not do, or full control of every event.

[YAML Blueprints](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/index.md), [Builder API](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/builder-api/index.md) and [Low-level API](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/low-level-api/index.md), the next three pages, describe each way in full.

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

Whichever way a model is written, it builds the same environment, and one run goes the same way from there. [How desflow Works](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/how-desflow-works/index.md) shows that run and each part it passes through.

# YAML Blueprints

A YAML blueprint is a simulation written as a file. This page shows how to run one, how a file is read and checked, how to change settings per environment, and where an error points. [YAML Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/yaml-keys/index.md) lists every key a blueprint accepts.

______________________________________________________________________

## What It Is

A blueprint holds, as data, the builder calls that a Python script would make. Each section becomes the builder call of the same name: `resources` is `add_resource`, `tasks` is `@app.task`, `stats` is `with_stats`, and so on. There is no second way of building: `SimulationContext.from_yaml` makes those calls, in the order a script would, and returns an ordinary `SimulationContext`. A blueprint and a script that make the same calls produce the same simulation, and the tests check that the YAML, builder and low-level versions of every example publish the same records.

Use Python for logic that YAML cannot express. Reference it with `!python`, as [Call Python from YAML](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/yaml-advanced/index.md) shows. An editor completes keys and marks a misspelt key or a value of the wrong kind as you type, from the JSON Schema that `desflow schema` prints and this site publishes. [Set Up Your Editor](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/set-up-your-editor/index.md) shows the setting.

______________________________________________________________________

## How to Use It

### Run a Blueprint

Run it from a shell with the `desflow` command, which the package installs. These lines use the local example:

```bash
desflow examples get local --api yaml    # downloads local/yaml/local.yaml
cd local/yaml
desflow run local.yaml                   # runs until run.until
desflow run local.yaml --until 10min     # overrides run.until
desflow run local.yaml --seed 7          # overrides simulation.random_seed
desflow examples                         # lists the other examples
desflow --version
```

`--until` takes seconds or a duration such as `10 min`, `2 hours` or `1 week`. The command logs at INFO level. `ConsoleEgress`, in its default `log` format, writes each batch at that level, so its output is visible. A run with no seed logs the seed it drew, with the command that repeats it. An invalid file prints its errors and exits with code 1.

Or run it from Python:

```python
from desflow import SimulationContext

app = SimulationContext.from_yaml("local.yaml")
app.run()  # calls run.before, then runs until run.until
```

`run()` calls the blueprint's `run.before` functions first, and uses `run.until` when no `until` is passed. The builder methods and decorators still work on the context `from_yaml` returns.

`load_context` loads a blueprint or a builder Python file by the same path, so a script that takes either kind of file needs no check of its own:

```python
from desflow import load_context

# A blueprint, or a builder Python file that defines a SimulationContext at
# module level, from its folder: the one loader desflow run and explain use
app = load_context(".", "local.yaml")
```

### Preview the Records

`desflow run FILE` builds the blueprint and runs it with its own sinks until `--until`, `run.until` or Ctrl+C. It takes a YAML file, and with `--sample` also a Python builder file, which prints its first events the same way. A builder file otherwise runs with `python FILE`. Two options print the records instead of sending them to the file's sinks:

| Command                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `desflow run FILE --sample N` | Prints the first `N` events, then stops. `N` is 1 or more. The run is unpaced: `factor` is set to 0 and `go_live_at` is cleared. `logical_start_time` and `random_seed` are kept, so timestamps and values look as they would in the real run. Ingress entries and `run.before` are skipped. Telemetry records print between the events but are not counted, and `system.simulation.lag_seconds` is not printed. |
| `desflow run FILE --stdout`   | Prints every record of a normal run except the `system.simulation.lag_seconds` readings, which describe the wall clock, not the model. `factor`, `go_live_at`, `logical_start_time` and ingress are kept; `run.before` is skipped.                                                                                                                                                                               |

Both replace every egress entry with one `Console` of `format: json`, and a second one for labels when the file has a `when: labels` entry. A JSON console writes each record as one JSON line on stdout. The run's log stays on stderr, so `desflow run FILE --sample 10 | jq .value` reads only the records.

A preview checks the whole file, but not the connectors it leaves out:

- The structure, keys and names of the whole file are validated.
- `run.before` is skipped, because its functions prepare the real sinks, such as creating topics. A warning on stderr says so when the file has any.
- The connectors a preview replaces or skips are not built, so only their `type` is checked. Their `config` is checked only by a run that builds them, such as `desflow run FILE` without these options.

| Combination                                           | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--sample` with `--stdout`                            | Allowed. `--stdout` adds nothing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `--sample` with `--until`, or a file with `run.until` | The run ends at whichever comes first. When `until` comes first, stderr says `sample ended at until with k of N events`. A model that runs out of events first ends the sample too, with exit code 0 and `sample ended with no events left, with k of N events`. |
| `--sample` on a file with `go_live_at`                | A backfill-then-live file prints its first history events. `when: history` and `when: live` have no effect, because their entries are replaced.                                                                                                                  |
| `--sample` on a file that publishes no events         | It runs until `until` or Ctrl+C, printing telemetry.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `--stdout` on a file with several egress entries      | One console prints each record once. Per-entry `batch_size` and `flush_interval` are dropped with the entries, and the `batching` section applies.                                                                                                               |
| `--sample` or `--stdout` with `--replications`        | Usage error, exit code 2: both print one run.                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `--sample 0`                                          | Usage error, exit code 2.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

[Command Line](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/index.md) lists every command and option.

### Times and Durations

A time in a blueprint is a number of seconds or a duration such as `90 s`, `10 min`, `2 hours` or `1 week`: `run.until`, a scenario step's `at`, `simulation.warmup`, a stats `interval`, and every time-valued distribution parameter. `rate` is the exception: it is a number per second. A text that is a plain number, such as `5` or `1e-3`, is that many seconds. A time place refuses NaN, `true` and a negative number, with the place named in the error. Infinity is refused where a time must end, such as `factor`, `initial_time`, a scenario `at` and a segment `every`, and elsewhere it means no limit. `factor` is a number, not a time, so `"2 min"` is refused.

`logical_start_time` and `go_live_at` are instants: `now`, a signed duration from now such as `-1d` or `-10m`, or an ISO datetime such as `2026-01-01T00:00:00`. Both are read against one moment, when the file is loaded, so `-10m` and `now` are exactly ten minutes apart. `now`, the relative forms and an ISO datetime without an offset are read in `simulation.timezone`, UTC by default, as [Clocks and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#time-zone) describes.

### Settings per Environment

`${VAR}` in a value is replaced with the environment variable, so one file can serve several environments. `${VAR:-default}` uses the default when the variable is unset or empty, as in a shell, and `$${` writes a literal `${`. An unquoted value is read as YAML reads it after the replacement, so `factor: ${SIM_FACTOR:-0}` is the number 0. A quoted value stays a string, so `"${LIMIT:-5}"` is the text `5`: write a number or a boolean unquoted. An unset variable with no default stops the load, and the error names its line.

```yaml
# Settings that change per environment, read from environment variables.
# Run it with: SIM_FACTOR=1 desflow run environment.yaml
simulation:
  sim_id: ${SIM_ID:-Shop}
  # An unquoted value is read after the replacement, so this is the number 0
  factor: ${SIM_FACTOR:-0}
  # Read against the moment the file is loaded: a day of history up to now
  logical_start_time: -1d
  # Under simulation: timestamps written in Melbourne time, with its offset; the
  # start and now are read in it. UTC by default
  timezone: ${SIM_TIMEZONE:-Australia/Melbourne}
  # Under simulation: how far the run is behind the wall clock, every 10 s; by
  # default off at factor 0 and every second otherwise, and 0 turns it off
  lag_interval: 10 s
  # Under simulation: true by default for a paced run and false at factor 0; false
  # lets a live run go on when a slow sink makes it fall behind the wall clock
  strict: false

egress:
  - {type: Console}

resources:
  # Quoted, because ${...} inside {...} would end the mapping early; the check
  # turns the text into a number
  packers: {current_cap: "${PACKERS:-2}", max_cap: 5}

run:
  # A duration, such as 1 week, or a number of seconds
  until: ${RUN_FOR:-1 hour}
```

The [Parquet example](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/parquet/index.md) switches from the local disk to S3 with five variables, and [Queues and Capacity](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/first-model/queues-and-capacity/index.md) runs one file with several numbers of packers.

### Include a File

`!include path` puts a mapping from another YAML file in place, such as the settings `desflow fit` writes: `packing: !include fitted/packing.yaml`. The path is relative to the file that names it. `!include {file: path, spawn: pack}` adds keys to the file's mapping, such as the task an arrival spawns. The file is read with the same loader, so `${VAR}`, `!python` and `!include` work in it. A file that includes itself, directly or through another file, is refused. [Input Fitting](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/input-fitting/#load-the-settings) shows it.

### Generated Values

A value place takes a constant or a generator, a mapping with a `gen` key. The places are `payload`, `attributes`, `set`, a store's `items`, the `value` of an `on:` entry, a `fire`, a timeout and a scenario step, an interrupt's `cause`, and a scenario `record`. [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/index.md) lists every kind, and [Generate Data](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/generate-data/choices-and-numbers/index.md) shows them in tasks. This blueprint builds an order record from most of them. The task's own keys come first:

```yaml
# Named values, drawn in order once for each instance of the task when it starts,
# because on_start is given. A generator reads one as {gen: var, name: ...}
vars:
  quantity: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 6]}
  unit_price: {gen: uniform, low: 5, high: 40, decimals: 2}
  ship_to:
    gen: object
    fields:
      city: {gen: one_of, choices: [Perth, Hobart]}
      postcode: {gen: integer, bounds: [1000, 9999]}
# Drawn once for each entity and task, at its first use
vars_once:
  region: {gen: one_of, choices: [north, south]}
# Published as one event record when the task starts
on_start:
  opened_at: {gen: now}
# Drawn after the service, and may read the vars
finish_vars:
  closed_at: {gen: now, offset: 1 min}
# The key of the task's records, drawn at the first record
key: {gen: sequence, start: 1, format: "order-{}"}
# Rows kept for a lookup or aggregate of this task by other tasks
history: 500
```

The rules for where a generator counts:

- **Depth.** In a `payload`, `set`, `attributes` or scenario `record`, a mapping with a `gen` key is a generator at any depth. A `gen` key directly under `set`, `attributes` or a `record` is a field name. A nested mapping keeps any key other than `gen`, such as a number or a date.
- **Data.** `{gen: literal, value: ...}` keeps a mapping as data. A mapping with no `gen` key in an `on:` or `fire` value is data, and a generator nested in it, or a nested `gen` inside an `on:` value, is stored as written. A mapping or list in a `put.item` is read as a payload is, so a generator nested at any depth is evaluated as the put is made.
- **Text.** Text in a value place stays text. `"attr.k * 3"` is that string, and `{gen: expr, expr: "attr.k * 3"}` evaluates it.
- **Files.** A `row` reads its file from the blueprint's folder when the file loads. A cell of digits is a number, so leading zeros are lost: write them with `{gen: format, template: "{n:05d}"}`.
- **Seeds.** Each generator draws from a random stream of its own, made from the run's seed and the generator's place in the file. Adding a field to a mapping moves no other generator's draws. Inserting an item into a list, a scenario step or an `on:` entry moves the draws of the items after it. Each `fake` has its own Faker, and a `sample` of a service draws from the generator's own stream, so the service's draws stay as they were.

The payload of the same task uses the other kinds. Each block below is a part of the same file.

Arithmetic takes a list of arguments, each a constant or a generator: `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `min` and `max`. `decimals` rounds the result. `expr` evaluates an expression whose `names` are generators.

```yaml
total:
  gen: add
  args: [{gen: var, name: unit_price}, 10]
  decimals: 1
discount:
  gen: subtract
  args: [100, {gen: var, name: quantity}]
weight:
  gen: multiply
  args: [{gen: var, name: quantity}, 2.5]
  decimals: 1
share:
  gen: divide
  args: [{gen: var, name: quantity}, 4]
  decimals: 2
least:
  gen: min
  args: [{gen: var, name: quantity}, 5]
most:
  gen: max
  args: [{gen: var, name: quantity}, 5]
```

```yaml
with_tax:
  gen: expr
  expr: "quantity * price * (1 + tax)"
  names:
    price: {gen: var, name: unit_price}
    tax: {gen: param, path: Shop.variables.tax_rate}
  decimals: 2
```

`lower`, `upper` and `literal` give text. `literal` keeps a value as data, even a mapping that has a `gen` key.

```yaml
region:
  gen: upper
  value: {gen: var, name: region}
source: {gen: lower, value: WEB}
note: {gen: literal, value: "n/a"}
```

`uniform` and `normal` draw numbers, and `sample` draws from a distribution or from a service of the file, with the service's own parameters.

```yaml
price: {gen: uniform, low: 5, high: 40, decimals: 2}
```

```yaml
delivery_minutes: {gen: normal, mean: 120, std: 15, decimals: 1}
```

```yaml
wait: {gen: sample, service: packing, decimals: 1}
retries: {gen: sample, dist: geometric, p: 0.5}
fixed: {gen: sample, dist: constant, value: 3}
```

`one_of` picks one value and `pick` picks `count` different values.

```yaml
colour: {gen: one_of, choices: [red, green, blue]}
```

```yaml
extras: {gen: pick, choices: [card, ribbon, box, tag], count: 2}
```

`weighted` picks by weight, from `options` or from a list of `value` and `weight`.

```yaml
paid_by:
  gen: weighted
  options: {card: 60, cash: 40}
priority:
  gen: weighted
  choices:
    - {value: normal, weight: 9}
    - {value: rush, weight: 1}
```

`sequence` counts from `start` in steps of `step`, starts again after `loop_after` values, and writes each with `format`.

```yaml
number: {gen: sequence, start: 1000, step: 5, loop_after: 1000, format: "ord-{}"}
```

`uuid` gives version 4 or 7.

```yaml
reference: {gen: uuid, version: 7}
```

`boolean` is true with probability `p`.

```yaml
gift: {gen: boolean, p: 0.1}
```

`now` gives the logical time, and `offset` moves it.

```yaml
due_at: {gen: now, offset: 1 hour}
```

`format_time` writes a time in a zone.

```yaml
placed_at:
  gen: format_time
  time: {gen: now, offset: -1 h}
  format: "%H:%M"
  tz: Australia/Melbourne
```

`fake` calls a method of Faker, with `args` and `kwargs`, for a `locale`.

```yaml
customer: {gen: fake, method: name, locale: en_AU}
phone: {gen: fake, method: numerify, args: ["04## ### ###"]}
email:
  gen: fake
  method: email
  kwargs: {domain: example.com}
```

`format` fills a `template` from `names`.

```yaml
code:
  gen: format
  template: "{region}-{n}"
  names:
    region: {gen: var, name: region}
    n: {gen: integer, bounds: [10, 99]}
```

`switch` and `when` choose a value from another.

```yaml
band:
  gen: switch
  on: {gen: var, name: quantity}
  cases:
    - {max: 3, value: small}
    - {min: 3, max: 5, value: medium}
  default: large
```

```yaml
size_label: {gen: when, condition: "quantity > 3", then: large, else: small}
```

`repeat` makes a list.

```yaml
scores:
  gen: repeat
  times: 3
  value: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 5]}
```

`var` and `attr` read a var and an attribute, or one `path` of it. `param` reads a live registry value, or one `field` of a mapping. `object` builds a mapping.

```yaml
city: {gen: var, name: ship_to, path: city}
size: {gen: attr, name: size}
slot: {gen: attr, name: delivery, path: slot}
```

```yaml
tax_rate: {gen: param, path: Shop.variables.tax_rate}
high: {gen: param, path: Shop.variables.limits, field: high}
```

```yaml
address:
  gen: object
  fields:
    street: {gen: fake, method: street_name}
    postcode: {gen: integer, bounds: [1000, 9999]}
```

`call` runs a function of your own, with `kwargs` worked out first.

```yaml
gross:
  gen: call
  function: !python generated_values_logic.with_tax
  kwargs:
    price: {gen: var, name: unit_price}
```

`row` takes a row of a CSV or Parquet file, kept by `where`, chosen by the column `weight`, and ending as `on_end` says:

```yaml
stocked:
  gen: row
  file: generated_values_products.csv
  where: stock > 0
  weight: share
  on_end: loop
```

Any generator can be null, left out, or made to give each value once:

```yaml
coupon: {gen: uuid, null_rate: 0.3}
gift_card: {gen: integer, bounds: [1000, 9999], omit_rate: 0.5}
rush_fee: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 9], omit_when: "quantity < 4"}
ticket: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 1000000], unique: true}
```

The first records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'order-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'opened_at': '2026-01-01T00:01:00.000+00:00'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'order-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'total': 21.1, 'discount': 99, 'weight': 2.5, 'share': 0.25, 'least': 1, 'most': 5, 'with_tax': 13.28, 'region': 'SOUTH', 'source': 'web', 'note': 'n/a', 'price': 9.17, 'delivery_minutes': 124.0, 'wait': 41.4, 'retries': 2, 'fixed': 3, 'colour': 'red', 'extras': ['box', 'card'], 'paid_by': 'card', 'priority': 'normal', 'number': 'ord-1000', 'reference': '019b76db-9260-735c-8c03-5157b422dbdd', 'gift': False, 'due_at': '2026-01-01T01:01:00.000+00:00', 'placed_at': '10:01', 'customer': 'Sara Mitchell', 'phone': '0403 164 579', 'email': 'kevinellis@example.com', 'code': 'south-67', 'band': 'small', 'size_label': 'small', 'scores': [3, 4, 5], 'city': 'Perth', 'size': 30, 'slot': 12, 'tax_rate': 0.2, 'high': 9, 'address': {'street': 'Paul Route', 'postcode': 9495}, 'gross': 13.28, 'stocked': {'sku': 'B-300', 'name': 'Bowl', 'stock': 7, 'share': 2}, 'coupon': '6ef12d5b-d11e-4079-a284-bcb0d3fbe634', 'gift_card': 3256, 'ticket': 940200}}
```

### Names an Expression Reads

An expression reads names, calls and operators, and nothing else. The names depend on where the expression sits, and [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/index.md) shows them in a task:

- **Run:** `t` (the clock), `registry["..."]`, `level.<name>`, `users.<name>`, `queue.<name>`, `signal.<name>.count` and `.processed`, `done_count` in a `when` group, and `handle.<n>.triggered`, `.processed`, `.ok`, `.value` and `.alive` for an opened event.
- **Entity and flow:** `attr.<name>`, `payload.<field>`, `process.key`, `process.flow_name`, `item` and `item_priority` after a `get`, `arg.<name>` from the `args` of a `wait` `task` branch or a `spawn`, `cause.<name>` in an interrupt, and `wait.<branch>.done`. `wait.suspend.value` reads in the task that was suspended, and `cause.<name>` in a task that `on_interrupt_run` reaches.
- **Task that routed here:** `upstream.<field>`, and `upstream.status` and `upstream.reason` in a task that `on_fail`, `on_renege` or `on_balk` reaches.
- **Calls on the model:** `held(r)`, `waiting(r)`, `putting(x)` and `getting(x)` give lists of mappings with an `entity`. A resource entry also has `rank`, `time`, `preempt`, `key` and `since`, a store put has `item`, and a container has `amount`. `running(task[, cond])` is a count, and `peek()` is the time of the next event.
- **Forms:** `[...]`, `{...}`, a list comprehension with one `for`, subscripts and slices, `is None`, `in`, and dotted reads at any depth. `payload['total']` is refused because `payload` is not a name by itself: write `payload.total`. `attr["class"]` reads an attribute whose name Python keeps as a word.
- **Functions:** `len`, `sum`, `sorted`, `range` (at most 1,000,000 items), `any`, `all`, `str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `abs`, one-argument and many-argument `min` and `max`, `round`, `floor`, `ceil`, `sqrt`, `exp`, `log`, `log10`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `has(attr.x)`, and `get_key(mapping, key, default)`, `set_key` and `drop_key`.

The limits are these. One reading that makes more than 1,000,000 items in all is a named run failure. `%` on text and `**` with an integer power above 10000 are refused, and so is `**` with a negative base and a fractional exponent, `round(x, -n)` with a very large `n`, and an expression nested more than 200 levels. Text is allowed in comparisons, indexes, list and mapping entries, `+` and the key functions. `prod` and `sumprod` are reserved for a later release, and a var, loop name or generator `names` entry cannot take them or any other name an expression already uses.

### Run on Your Own Environment

`simulation.environment` runs the model on your own subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`, named with `!python`, as `SimulationContext(environment=...)` does in Python, for example `environment: !python my_model.TracingEnvironment`.

A subclass that overrides `__init__` takes `**kwargs` and passes them on, because desflow builds it with the arguments it builds its own environment with. One that overrides `schedule` or `step` calls `super()`. When a script steps outside `run()`, `step` runs once per model event. Inside `run()`, it runs once per event, desflow's own events included.

In a blueprint, the class is named under `simulation`. `CountingEnvironment` in `endings_logic.py` counts the events the run processes:

```yaml
# Run on a subclass of DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, from endings_logic.py beside the
# file
environment: !python endings_logic.CountingEnvironment
```

______________________________________________________________________

## How It Works

`from_yaml` makes the builder calls for you, so a blueprint gets everything [the builder does](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/builder-api/#how-it-works), and it checks the whole file before anything runs. A file is read and checked in five steps, and any step that fails stops the load with a `BlueprintError` before anything runs:

1. **Read the file.** `read_document` reads it with a subclass of `yaml.SafeLoader`. `${VAR}` is replaced while each scalar is read, `!python module.attribute` imports the module and returns the attribute, `!include path` reads a mapping from another YAML file relative to this one, and every key's line is kept in a source map. Every other node is built as `yaml.safe_load` would build it. A key written twice in one mapping is refused at its second line, and the error names both lines.
1. **Check every field.** The document is validated against the `Blueprint` model. Unknown keys are refused, so a misspelt key is reported rather than ignored. Every distribution is built as the builder would build it, so a parameter out of range, `true`, NaN, or one the family does not take, is refused here. Every expression place is checked at its line, a capacity below 0 is refused, and a refusal under a field that takes a name or a mapping reports only the member that matches, with no type or class name. Every relative time is read against one `now`. A `spawn` `after` and a `fire` `after` must be above 0. `simulation.environment` must be a subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`. All validation errors are reported at once.
1. **Check the names.** Each name in the file must exist and fit where it is used:
   - Every service, resource, store, container and next task that a task names exists.
   - Every task's `spawn` and `on:` spawn names a task that does not share an arrival's name.
   - A `subscribe` names a task or a signal.
   - An `on:` fire names a signal, and an `on:` interrupt names a task.
   - An `on:` `fire ... from` names a signal or a task. The task must run on the same entity as the `on:` list. For a task's list, that is the entity of the task that holds the list. For a signal's list, it is the entity of a task that fires the signal.
   - Every `level.<name>` in an expression names a store or a container, and every `users.<name>` and `queue.<name>` names a resource.
   - A name is used in one of resources, stores, containers and signals, and holds no dot or space.
   - A task's `priority` needs a resource with `queue: priority`.
   - Resources and stores have whole-number capacities.
   - An `on:` fire with `urgent`, `after` or `priority` names a signal with `once: true`. A `priority` is a whole number and is refused with `urgent`.
   - A `fail` is refused with `from`, and `defused` needs `fail`. A `fail_reason` needs a `fail` condition.
   - A `listen` names one of `signal` and `handle`, an `index` needs a `handle`, and the signal or handle is declared.
   - A `when` or a generator `value` in a signal's `on:` that reads `wait.<branch>` is refused, because a signal's entries run with no wait in scope. So is an `each.index` or `each.value` read outside the branch of an `each`.
   - `simulation.environment` names a subclass of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`.
1. **Build the context.** The builder calls are made in the order a script would make them: the simulation, ingress, egress, batching, stats, resources, stores, containers, variables, services, arrivals, tasks, arrival loops, processes, telemetry and the scenario.
1. **Check the paths.** The parameters are registered into a scratch registry, with the code that the run uses. Every scenario `path`, and every `registry["..."]` that an expression reads, is then checked against the paths the run will have. Every scenario `value` must convert to the type its path holds.

`!python module.attribute` imports `module` and returns its `attribute`: a function, a class, a dictionary or a constant. The longest prefix that is a module is imported, and the rest is read as attributes. The folder of the YAML file is added to the front of `sys.path`, so a module beside the blueprint is found from any working directory. `${VAR}` is replaced inside a reference too. Every reference is resolved when the file is loaded, so a wrong one fails before the run starts, with the file and line:

______________________________________________________________________

## Stability and Limits

An error at any step is mapped back to its line through the source map. A time in a message reads `5` for a whole number, and a number in `{now:g}` form has six significant digits, so 1000000 reads `1e+06`:

```yaml
# A blueprint with a mistake, for the YAML Blueprints page: pack_order has a priority,
# but its resource serves its queue in the default order, fifo.
simulation: {sim_id: Shop, factor: 0}

resources:
  packers: {current_cap: 1, max_cap: 2}

services:
  packing: {dist: constant, value: 1.5 s}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.5, spawn: pack_order}

tasks:
  pack_order:
    service: packing
    resource: packers
    priority: 0
    payload: {event_type: order_packed}
```

```python
try:
    SimulationContext.from_yaml("blueprint_error.yaml")
except BlueprintError as error:
    print(f"Error: {error}")  # what desflow run prints, before exiting with code 1
```

```text
Error: blueprint_error.yaml:18: task 'pack_order' has a priority, but resource 'packers' does not set queue: priority; set it, or remove the priority
```

A blueprint covers configuration, including several resources per task (`resource: [picker, bench]` and `keep`), preemption (`preempt: true`) and breakdowns (`breakdown:`). These stay in Python:

- **Values computed per entity.** A mapping payload is a constant, apart from three values added for each entity: the task id that `id_field` adds, the attributes that `attributes` adds, and the item a `get` took, which `item_field` adds. Random choices, derived fields and state carried between events are a Python payload or process, as [Call Python from YAML](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/yaml-advanced/index.md) shows. A task's `priority` and a `get` or `put` amount can be an expression. `next` rules read attributes, payload fields, levels, registry values, the item a `get` took (`item.<field>`), the wait's branches (`wait.<branch>.done`) and signals (`signal.<name>.count`), as [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/index.md) describes.
- **Keys described where their subject is.** `seize`, `release`, `open`, `cancel` and handles are in [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/index.md) and [Tasks and Processes](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/index.md). `batch` is in [Serve Entities Together](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/serve-entities-together/index.md). `family` and `members` are in [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/index.md). `{of, key}` and `{of, lowest}` references, `fire` with `fail`, and `listen` are in [Signals and Waiting](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/index.md). `lookup`, `previous`, `upstream` and `aggregate` are in [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/index.md). `breakdown.clock` is in [Priority and Preemption](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/priority-and-preemption/index.md). The arrival keys are in [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/index.md), and `run.segments`, `steps` and `sync` in [Run Length](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#run-in-segments).
- **Entity keys.** An arrival's `key` and a task's `key` take text, a number or a generator, and the default is `<arrival>-<n>`. Only a key written as a Python function is builder only.
- **One simulation per file.** A blueprint has one `sim_id`. `!include` puts a mapping from another file in place, such as fitted settings, but not a second simulation.

### Security

A blueprint with no `!python` references is read entirely by `yaml.SafeLoader`, and loading it imports only the connector modules its `type` entries name. An `!include` reads another YAML file the same way and imports nothing itself. A file that references Python, directly or in a file it includes, runs the imports it names. Such a file needs the same trust as a Python script: run blueprints only from people whose scripts you would run. Every other node is built by `yaml.SafeLoader`, and only `!python` and `!include` are added to it.

# Builder API

This page writes a whole simulation as one Python file with the builder, `SimulationContext`: a shop that packs orders with boxes from stock, prints a label, and leaves the parcel for a courier. It builds on [Writing a Model](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/index.md), which places the builder between a blueprint and the low-level API, and on [Tasks and Processes](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/index.md), which describes what a task does.

______________________________________________________________________

## What It Is

The builder works in two phases. You describe the simulation with its methods and decorators, and nothing runs. `run()` then builds the environment and the connectors and starts the clock:

Until `run()` builds the environment, the runtime helpers `context.spawn`, `context.call`, `context.signal`, `context.get_resource`, `context.get_store`, `context.get_container` and `context.env` raise `RuntimeError`. Loops, tasks and processes run only after that, so the helpers belong inside them.

______________________________________________________________________

## How to Use It

### Create the Context

The context names the simulation and sets its clock: `factor` for the pacing, `random_seed` for the draws, `logical_start_time` for the timestamps. It also takes `go_live_at` and `warmup`, which [Time and Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/index.md) describes.

```python
app = SimulationContext(
    sim_id="Shop",
    factor=0.0,  # 0.0 unpaced, 1.0 real time
    random_seed=42,  # the same draws on every run
    logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 10, 1, 9, 0),  # what simulation time 0 is
)
```

### Declare Resources, Stores and Containers

A task holds a resource while it works. A container holds an amount and a store holds items, and tasks take from and add to both. `add_variable` registers any other live value. [Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/index.md) and [Stores and Containers](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/stores-and-containers/index.md) describe each.

```python
app.add_resource("packers", current_cap=2, max_cap=5)  # 2 packers now, room for 5
app.add_container("boxes", current_cap=200, max_cap=200, level=100)  # an amount
app.add_store("parcels", current_cap=20, max_cap=50)  # items, waiting for a courier
app.add_variable("conveyor_speed", 1.5)  # any other live value
```

### Add Distributions

Each service is a distribution, given its parameters by keyword. Each arrival is a distribution too, and [Start Them from Arrivals](#start-them-from-arrivals) adds it with the task it starts. A parameter out of range, or one the family does not take, raises `ValueError` here, before the run. [Arrivals and Services](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/index.md) lists the ten families.

```python
app.add_service("packing", dist="triangular", low=1, mode=2, high=4)
app.add_service("labelling", dist="constant", value=0.5)
```

### Write the Tasks

`@app.task` turns a function into a task: it publishes `queued`, waits for its resource and its `get`, publishes `started`, waits the service time, adds its `put`, and publishes what the function returns as the finished event. `next` names the task that follows, and the function receives `upstream`, `entity` or `item` when it declares them. [Task Flow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/index.md) covers rules and weights.

```python
@app.task(
    service_id="packing",
    resource_id="packers",
    get={"container": "boxes", "amount": 1},  # one box, once it has a packer
    next="print_label",  # the task that follows
)
def pack_order(task_id: int):
    # The value of the finished event: exactly this dictionary
    return {"event_type": "order_packed"}


@app.task(service_id="labelling", put={"store": "parcels"})  # a timed step
def print_label(task_id: int, upstream):
    # upstream is what pack_order handed on; the payload becomes the parcel
    return {"event_type": "label_printed", "packed_by": upstream.task_id}


@app.task(get={"store": "parcels"})
def collect(task_id: int, item):
    return {"event_type": "parcel_collected", "label": item["event_type"]}
```

### Start Them from Arrivals

`add_arrival` with `spawn=` is the builder form of YAML's `spawn`: each arrival starts the named task for its entity, keyed `orders-1`, `orders-2` and so on. The record's `instance` comes from the task's one counter, which `next` and other arrivals share, so no two runs of the task share an id. A `spawn` that names a task never added is refused when `run()` checks the model.

```python
# An order every 2 s on average, keyed orders-1, ..., each starting pack_order
app.add_arrival("orders", dist="exponential", rate=0.5, spawn="pack_order")
app.add_arrival("couriers", dist="constant", value=10, spawn="collect")  # every 10 s
```

`@app.arrival_loop` runs a generator of your own that waits with `context.wait_for_arrival` and starts tasks with `context.spawn`. A loop is needed only when it does more than start one task, such as choosing the task from the entity's attributes. [Tasks and Processes](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#arrivals-start-tasks) shows a loop that does what `spawn=` does, written by hand.

### Arguments for the Keys of a Blueprint

Every key of a [blueprint](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/index.md) has a builder argument of the same meaning. This script uses the ones that shape what an arrival and a task start with:

```python
app = SimulationContext(
    sim_id="Shop",
    factor=0.0,
    random_seed=42,
    logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
)
app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
app.add_resource("packers", current_cap=1, max_cap=2)
app.add_service("packing", dist="constant", value=20)
app.add_arrival(
    "orders",
    gap="30 s",  # a number, a duration, an expression or a generator
    first_at=5,  # the first gap ends at 5 s; a time in the past arrives at once
    max_events=4,  # stops itself after the fourth start; needs a spawn
    vars={"size": generator({"gen": "integer", "bounds": [1, 5]})},  # read by key
    key=generator({"gen": "sequence", "format": "order-{}"}),
    attributes={"size": generator({"gen": "var", "name": "size"})},
    spawn="pack_order",
)
```

A generator is written with `generator({...})`, and a payload with `Template(...)`, both from `desflow.values`. `Template` takes `vars=` and `vars_once=` as a task's `vars` and `vars_once` do. The task side:

```python
payload = Template(
    {"size": {"gen": "attr", "name": "size"}, "shift": {"gen": "var", "name": "shift"}},
    vars={"label": {"gen": "uuid"}},  # drawn for each instance of the task
    vars_once={
        "shift": {"gen": "one_of", "choices": ["early", "late"]}
    },  # for each entity
)


@app.task(
    service_id="packing",
    resource_id="packers",
    history=100,  # rows kept for a Template or an aggregate that looks this task up
    next="record",
)
def pack_order(task_id: int):
    return payload


@app.task()
def record(task_id: int, upstream):
    return NO_RECORD  # the task runs and publishes no finished record
```

The first order starts at 5 s, then one starts every 30 s, and the fourth is the last. The keys are `order-0` to `order-3`. `record` runs but publishes no finished record.

A resource a task waits for can have its own queue order, a family of members, and a signal that wakes the task. This script holds a unit of `bench` by priority, gives up after 15 s, opens a request for one desk and cancels it, and listens for a defused signal:

```python
app.add_resource("bench", current_cap=1, max_cap=1, queue="priority")
# One desk for each key: desk[0] and desk[1], made when the run starts
app.add_resource("desk", current_cap=1, family=True, members=2)
app.add_signal("closing", once=True, defused=True)
app.add_variable("closings_seen", 0)
```

```python
@app.task(
    # A name, or a mapping with priority, preempt and patience
    seize={"resource": "bench", "priority": 1, "preempt": "f", "patience": 15},
    service_time=18,
    release="bench",  # frees the oldest unit of bench the flow holds
    # A request for desk[1], opened as a handle, and cancelled again
    open={"spare": {"request": {"of": "desk", "key": 1}}},
    cancel="spare",
    on_renege="gave_up",  # the task a flow goes to after it leaves the line
    listen={
        "signal": "closing",
        "on": [{"path": "Shop.variables.closings_seen", "value": 1}],
    },
)
def pack(task_id: int):
    return {"event_type": "packed"}


@app.task()
def gave_up(task_id: int, upstream):
    return {"event_type": "left", "key": upstream.key}
```

An order arrives every 10 s and packing takes 18 s, so the third order waits from 30 s, passes its patience of 15 s at 45 s, and goes to `gave_up` with a record `{'event_type': 'left', 'key': 'orders-3'}`.

The other arguments follow the key of the same name:

| Call                  | Arguments                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `add_arrival`         | `group`, `active`, `off_mode`, `initial`, and the distribution parameters.                 |
| `add_arrival_replay`  | `time`, `unit`, `fields`, `on_invalid`, `active`, `off_mode`, `attributes`, `key`, `vars`. |
| `add_initial_arrival` | `initial` entities at the start, with `spawn`, `attributes`, `key`, `gap`, `vars`.         |
| `add_resource`        | `queue`, `preempt`, `queue_limit`, `type`, `family`, `members`.                            |
| `add_signal`          | `once`, `on`, `family`, `members`, `defused`.                                              |
| `with_stats`          | `level`, `interval`, `on_change`, `trace`.                                                 |
| `add_readings`        | `interval` and a mapping of reading names to expressions.                                  |
| `add_breakdown`       | `resource`, `time_to_failure`, `repair`, `work`, `clock`.                                  |
| `add_egress`          | `when`, `batch_size`, `flush_interval`, `envelope`.                                        |

A task takes the keys of a blueprint task as arguments too:

- **`seize`, `release`, `open`, `cancel`, `signal`, `interrupt`, `resume`.** A name or the same mapping as the key. A request that `open` makes has a `preempted` attribute, which is true once a higher priority took the unit.
- **`preempt`.** A boolean or a boolean word: `preempt="f"` is false, as in YAML.
- **`on_interrupt`, `on_interrupt_next`, `on_interrupt_run`.** `on_interrupt_run` and `resume` take the same forms as the keys of those names. `on_renege`, `on_balk` and `on_fail` take no extra argument.
- **`listen` and `fail_reason`.** `listen` is the mapping of the key. `fail_reason` is text, an expression or a generator. `add_signal(defused=True)` and the `on=` actions `fail`, `defused`, `priority` and `when` are the blueprint forms.
- **`spawn`.** A mapping with `task`, `count` (a number, an expression or a function), `copy_attributes` and `args`. `count` as text reads the run and the names of the running process.
- **`set_args`, `activate`, `deactivate`.** `set_args` writes values in the flow's own process arguments, after `set`. `activate` and `deactivate` switch on or off the arrivals the task names, in one name or a list.
- **`batch`.** The batching mapping of the key.
- **`history`, `Template` and `note_values`.** `history=` keeps rows for a task that a `Template` or an aggregate looks up. The builder does not scan a `Template` for the tasks it names, so `note_values("<task>", template)` tells it to, and gives the `Template` the full gate: its `payload`, `vars` and `vars_once` are searched, and the start is dropped before the function runs. Without it, a `Template` with a `lookup` of a task with no row drops the start after the task function has returned it. By then the `queued` and `started` records have been published, the item of a `get` has been consumed, and the units and `wait` requests are given back. The builder refuses an unknown lookup target, a task `note_values` names that does not exist, and a cycle. `note_values(task, *places)` also takes generators written in your own code, but not a set or an iterator.
- **`Transfer(item=)` and `Signal.processed`.** `Transfer(item=...)` is the item a store `put` adds: a constant, text or a generator, and `Signal.processed` is true once the signal has fired and its callbacks have run.

A `row` generator written in a script, through `generator(spec)` or a `Template`, is read from the working directory at the call that adds it: `add_arrival`, `add_arrival_replay`, `add_initial_arrival`, `add_store`, `add_scenario`, `add_step`, `add_signal` and `task`. A missing or unusable file raises `ValueError` there, naming the generator's place and the file. A blueprint reads the same files from its own folder. A `row` gives a mapping, so a place that needs a number or text takes it only inside another generator.

`with_stats(on_change=True)` also publishes a resource's readings right after each `request` and `release` call on it, and needs a level above `none`. `with_stats(trace=True)` publishes one `trace` record for each event the environment processes, to the sinks added with `add_egress(provider, when="trace")` and to no other, and `env.trace_events(False)` switches it off during a run. `add_breakdown(clock="calendar")` counts the time to failure from the start or the last repair, and `clock="busy"` counts it only while the resource holds a unit. `run(until, segments=..., steps=..., sync=...)` has the meaning of the YAML `run` keys, which [Run Length](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#run-in-segments) shows in the Builder tab.

### Measure the Run

`with_stats` switches on the built-in statistics, published as telemetry. [Statistics](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/index.md) lists the levels.

```python
app.with_stats("typical", interval=30)  # readings, counts, waits, every 30 s
```

### Add a Process

`add_process` is for anything that is not a task. It calls a generator with the context when the run starts. Here the process is a speed that drifts.

```python
def speed_drift(context: SimulationContext, step: float):
    """Raises the conveyor speed a little every 10 simulation seconds."""
    path = "Shop.variables.conveyor_speed"
    while True:
        yield context.env.timeout(10.0)
        speed = context.env.registry.get(path).value
        context.env.registry.update(path, speed + step)


app.add_process(speed_drift, step=0.1)
```

### Attach the Connectors

`add_ingress` brings parameter changes in, and `add_egress` writes records out, each with its own batching if it needs it. [Ingress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/ingress/index.md) and [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/index.md) list the connectors.

```python
app.add_ingress(LocalIngress(schedule=[(5.0, "Shop.resources.packers.current_cap", 3)]))
app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress(), batch_size=100, flush_interval=1.0)
app.with_batching(batch_size=1_000, flush_interval=5.0)  # defaults for other sinks
```

`LocalIngress` counts its delays in wall-clock seconds, so the change to 3 packers is due 5 seconds after the run starts. This unpaced run ends in under a second, so the change never lands. At `factor=1.0`, it lands 5 seconds into the run. For a change at an exact simulation time, use a scenario step, `add_step(at, path=..., value=...)` or `add_scenario(steps)`, which [Live Parameters](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#script-an-experiment) describes. A process that waits and then updates the registry, as `speed_drift` above does, also works.

`compile_parameters()` returns the `SimParameter` that `run()` will register. Call it to check the registry paths before a run. A resource has three: `current_cap`, `max_cap` and `queue_limit`, which is `None` when unset. A limit changes through its path, `<sim_id>.resources.<name>.queue_limit`, in a scenario step, an `on:` action or a low-level `set`, and not by assigning `queue_limit`, which is read-only. The new limit applies from the next request, and a smaller one removes nobody who waits. A resource with its own `PutQueue` has no `queue_limit` path:

```python
paths = app.compile_parameters()  # the SimParameter that run() registers
```

### Run It

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(
        level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s [%(asctime)s] %(message)s"
    )
    app.run(until="2 min")
```

`app.on_change` takes callbacks that receive every parameter change of each run `start()` builds, as [Follow Every Change](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#follow-every-change) shows.

`ConsoleEgress` writes each batch of records in one INFO log call, one line per record, so the script switches logging on before it runs. Only the first line of a batch carries the logging format's prefix, such as the time and the level. The other lines are bare. The first events of the run:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 2.5523798766964667, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'queued'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 2.5523798766964667, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'started'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 2.695845327144759, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'queued'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 2.695845327144759, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'started'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 3.7373184714894925, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'queued'}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 4.019540612543443, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-4', 'task': 'pack_order', 'instance': 3, 'value': {'path_id': 'Shop.service.packing', 'sim_id': 'Shop', 'service': 'packing', 'status': 'queued'}}
```
