# lookup

`lookup`: a row of the finished payloads of the task `task`, or the part of it at `path` (dotted; an integer part indexes a list).

A row is readable from the instant the task's finished record is published. The task keeps its last `history` rows (default 1,000,000).

`strategy` is `random` (the default), `first` (the oldest row kept) or `last` (the newest). `histogram` splits the rows kept, in the order they were written, into bins of the stated shares; a draw picks a bin by its frequency and then a row of the bin at random, so it is for `random` only. A bin that holds no row yet is left out of the draw, and while no bin with a frequency above 0 holds a row (a few rows and a last bin of frequency 0), the draw is over all the rows. `latest_by` keeps only the newest row for each value of that field of the row, so a lookup sees a customer's latest address; `strategy` and `histogram` then choose among those rows, oldest first by the time each was written. `distinct` draws without replacement within one `repeat`, so the items of one order differ.

Use it for a value from a record that another task already published, such as an existing customer.

## Keys

| Key         | Type                                  | Default    |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `gen`       | `lookup`                              | required   |
| `task`      | text                                  | required   |
| `path`      | text                                  | none       |
| `strategy`  | `random` or `first` or `last`         | `"random"` |
| `histogram` | list of [HistogramBin](#histogrambin) | none       |
| `latest_by` | text                                  | none       |
| `distinct`  | boolean                               | `false`    |

Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

### HistogramBin

One bin of a `lookup` histogram: `bin` is the share of the rows it covers, in the order they were written, and `frequency` is the chance that a draw falls in it. Both are scaled to add up to 1, so `{bin: 2, frequency: 8}, {bin: 8, frequency: 2}` means the same as 0.2 with 0.8, and 0.8 with 0.2.

| Key         | Type   | Default  |
| ----------- | ------ | -------- |
| `bin`       | number | required |
| `frequency` | number | required |

## Example

Three customers start at time 0. Each order picks one of them at random and publishes its `customer_id`. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Lookup: a value from a finished record of another task.
# Three customers start at time 0, and an order starts every 60 seconds. The run lasts
# 200 seconds, so three orders start.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/lookup.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  customers: {initial: 3, dist: constant, value: 3600, spawn: customer}
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  customer:
    payload:
      customer_id: {gen: sequence, start: 100}
  order:
    payload:
      customer_id: {gen: lookup, task: customer, path: customer_id}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Lookup: a value from a finished record of another task, builder API.

The builder version of `lookup.yaml`. A task that something looks up keeps its finished
rows, so the customer task sets `history`.

Run it with: python examples/generators/lookup_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("customers", "constant", value=3600, spawn="customer", initial=3)
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    customer_payload = Template(
        {"customer_id": {"gen": "sequence", "start": 100}}, name="tasks.customer"
    )
    order_payload = Template(
        {"customer_id": {"gen": "lookup", "task": "customer", "path": "customer_id"}},
        name="tasks.order",
    )

    @app.task(name="customer", history=1_000_000)
    def customer(task_id):
        """Gives one customer."""
        return customer_payload

    @app.task(name="order")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return order_payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Lookup: a value from a finished record of another task, low-level API.

The low-level version of `lookup.yaml`: plain SimPy on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`,
which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each draw is made with
`Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's generator at that
place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The script keeps the `customer_id` of each
customer it has published, and an order takes one at an index drawn with
`integers(len(rows))`, as `lookup` does with `strategy: random`.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/lookup_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    seller = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.customer_id")
    customers: list = []  # the customer_id of each customer so far, oldest first

    def customer_arrivals():
        yield env.timeout(0)
        for number in range(1, 4):
            customers.append(100 + number - 1)
            env.publish_event(
                f"customers-{number}",
                {"customer_id": customers[-1]},
                task="customer",
                instance=number - 1,
            )

    def orders():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            payload = {"customer_id": customers[int(seller.integers(len(customers)))]}
            env.publish_event(
                f"orders-{number}", payload, task="order", instance=number - 1
            )

    env.process(customer_arrivals())
    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 0.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'customers-1', 'task': 'customer', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'customer_id': 100}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 0.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'customers-2', 'task': 'customer', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'customer_id': 101}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 0.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'customers-3', 'task': 'customer', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'customer_id': 102}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'customer_id': 102}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'customer_id': 101}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'customer_id': 101}}
```

## JSON Schema

The schema of `Lookup`, from `desflow schema`.

```json
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "`lookup`: a row of the finished payloads of the task `task`, or the part of it\nat `path` (dotted; an integer part indexes a list).\n\nA row is readable from the instant the task's finished record is published. The\ntask keeps its last `history` rows (default 1,000,000).\n\n`strategy` is `random` (the default), `first` (the oldest row kept) or `last` (the\nnewest). `histogram` splits the rows kept, in the order they were written, into\nbins of the stated shares; a draw picks a bin by its frequency and then a row of the\nbin at random, so it is for `random` only. A bin that holds no row yet is left out\nof the draw, and while no bin with a frequency above 0 holds a row (a few rows and\na last bin of frequency 0), the draw is over all the rows. `latest_by` keeps only\nthe newest row for each value of that field of the row, so a lookup sees a\ncustomer's latest address; `strategy` and `histogram` then choose among those rows,\noldest first by the time each was written. `distinct` draws without replacement\nwithin one `repeat`, so the items of one order differ.",
  "properties": {
    "null_rate": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "maximum": 1,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "number"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "unique": {
      "default": false,
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ]
    },
    "omit_rate": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "maximum": 1,
          "minimum": 0,
          "type": "number"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "omit_when": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "gen": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "const": "lookup",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ]
    },
    "task": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "path": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "strategy": {
      "default": "random",
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "enum": [
            "random",
            "first",
            "last"
          ],
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ]
    },
    "histogram": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "items": {
            "$ref": "#/$defs/HistogramBin"
          },
          "type": "array"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "latest_by": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "null"
        }
      ],
      "default": null
    },
    "distinct": {
      "default": false,
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/Placeholder"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "gen",
    "task"
  ],
  "title": "Lookup",
  "type": "object"
}
```

# previous

`previous`: the last finished payload of the same task for the same stream, or the part of it at `path`. The stream is the arrival, so all the entities it starts share one, except for an arrival with `count` or `keys`, where each entity has its own. `default` is evaluated only when the stream has no finished payload yet, and without one the first reading is null.

Use it for a value from the last finished record of the same task, such as the previous reading.

## Keys

| Key       | Type       | Default  |
| --------- | ---------- | -------- |
| `gen`     | `previous` | required |
| `path`    | text       | none     |
| `default` | Value      | none     |

A `Value` is a constant or a generator, as [What a Generator Is](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#what-a-generator-is) explains. Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

## Example

`before` is the `reading` of the order before, and 0 for the first order. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Previous: a value from the last finished record of the same task.
# An order starts every 60 seconds, and the run lasts 200 seconds, so three orders
# start.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/previous.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  order:
    payload:
      reading: {gen: integer, bounds: [10, 20]}
      before: {gen: previous, path: reading, default: 0}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Previous: a value from the last finished record of the same task, builder API.

The builder version of `previous.yaml`. The task keeps its last payload because its
template holds a `previous`.

Run it with: python examples/generators/previous_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    payload = Template(
        {
            "reading": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [10, 20]},
            "before": {"gen": "previous", "path": "reading", "default": 0},
        },
        name="tasks.order",
    )

    @app.task(name="order")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Previous: a value from the last finished record of the same task, low-level API.

The low-level version of `previous.yaml`: plain SimPy on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`,
which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each draw is made with
`Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's generator at that
place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The script keeps the last reading in a
variable, which is what `previous` reads, and uses the default 0 until there is one.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/previous_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    reading = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.reading")

    def orders():
        before = 0  # the default, until there is a finished record
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            payload = {"reading": int(reading.integers(10, 20 + 1)), "before": before}
            before = payload["reading"]
            env.publish_event(
                f"orders-{number}", payload, task="order", instance=number - 1
            )

    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'reading': 17, 'before': 0}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'reading': 16, 'before': 17}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'reading': 18, 'before': 16}}
```

```json
  "properties": {
```

# upstream

`upstream`: the finished payload of the task that routed to this one with `next`, or the part of it at `path`. A start by an arrival has no upstream, and a task that `on_fail` or `on_interrupt_next` reaches is handed a failure or an interrupted record, so a blueprint refuses `upstream` there.

Use it for a value from the record of the task that routed to this one.

## Keys

| Key    | Type       | Default  |
| ------ | ---------- | -------- |
| `gen`  | `upstream` | required |
| `path` | text       | none     |

Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

## Example

The task `order` routes to the task `invoice`, which publishes the amount of the order. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Upstream: a value from the record of the task that routed here.
# An order starts every 60 seconds and routes to an invoice. The run lasts 200 seconds,
# so three orders start.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/upstream.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  order:
    payload:
      amount: {gen: integer, bounds: [10, 20]}
    next: invoice
  invoice:
    payload:
      amount: {gen: upstream, path: amount}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Upstream: a value from the record of the task that routed here, builder API.

The builder version of `upstream.yaml`. The order routes to the invoice with `next`.

Run it with: python examples/generators/upstream_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    order_payload = Template(
        {"amount": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [10, 20]}}, name="tasks.order"
    )
    invoice_payload = Template(
        {"amount": {"gen": "upstream", "path": "amount"}}, name="tasks.invoice"
    )

    @app.task(name="order", next="invoice")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return order_payload

    @app.task(name="invoice")
    def invoice(task_id):
        """Gives the invoice of one order."""
        return invoice_payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Upstream: a value from the record of the task that routed here, low-level API.

The low-level version of `upstream.yaml`: plain SimPy on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`,
which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each draw is made with
`Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's generator at that
place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The order publishes its record, then the
invoice takes the amount from it, as `upstream` reads the record of the task that routed
to it.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/upstream_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    amount = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.amount")

    def orders():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            key, instance = f"orders-{number}", number - 1
            order = {"amount": int(amount.integers(10, 20 + 1))}
            env.publish_event(key, order, task="order", instance=instance)
            env.publish_event(
                key, {"amount": order["amount"]}, task="invoice", instance=instance
            )

    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text

[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'amount': 16}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'invoice', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'amount': 16}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'amount': 10}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'invoice', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'amount': 10}}
```

# aggregate

`aggregate`: `mean`, `sum`, `min`, `max` or `count` over the last `last` rows of the task `task` that `where` keeps. `where` is an expression over the row's own fields, such as `lead_days == 3 and precipitation > 0`; without it every row counts. `count` counts rows and takes no `path`; the others read the number at `path`. A reading looks back through the rows the task keeps (its `history`) until `last` rows are kept, and takes the rows there are when `where` keeps fewer.

Use it for a mean, sum, minimum, maximum or count over earlier records of another task.

## Keys

| Key        | Type                                         | Default  |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| `gen`      | `aggregate`                                  | required |
| `task`     | text                                         | required |
| `path`     | text                                         | none     |
| `last`     | integer                                      | required |
| `function` | `mean` or `sum` or `min` or `max` or `count` | required |
| `where`    | text                                         | none     |

Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

## Example

Three readings start at time 0. Each order publishes the mean of the last 3 levels. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Aggregate: a mean, sum, minimum, maximum or count over the finished records of another
# task. Three readings start at time 0, and an order starts every 60 seconds. The run
# lasts 200 seconds, so three orders start.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/aggregate.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  readings: {initial: 3, dist: constant, value: 3600, spawn: reading}
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  reading:
    payload:
      level: {gen: integer, bounds: [10, 20]}
  order:
    payload:
      average: {gen: aggregate, task: reading, path: level, last: 3, function: mean}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Aggregate: a mean, sum, minimum, maximum or count over the finished records of another
task, builder API.

The builder version of `aggregate.yaml`. A task that something aggregates keeps its
finished rows, so the reading task sets `history`.

Run it with: python examples/generators/aggregate_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("readings", "constant", value=3600, spawn="reading", initial=3)
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    reading_payload = Template(
        {"level": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [10, 20]}}, name="tasks.reading"
    )
    order_payload = Template(
        {
            "average": {
                "gen": "aggregate",
                "task": "reading",
                "path": "level",
                "last": 3,
                "function": "mean",
            }
        },
        name="tasks.order",
    )

    @app.task(name="reading", history=1_000_000)
    def reading(task_id):
        """Gives one reading."""
        return reading_payload

    @app.task(name="order")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return order_payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Aggregate: a mean, sum, minimum, maximum or count over the finished records of another
task, low-level API.

The low-level version of `aggregate.yaml`: plain SimPy on a
`DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`, which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each
draw is made with `Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's
generator at that place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The script keeps the level of
each reading it has published, and an order takes the mean of the last 3, as `aggregate`
does with `function: mean`.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/aggregate_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    level = sampler.generator("tasks.reading.payload.level")
    levels: list = []  # the level of each reading so far, oldest first

    def reading_arrivals():
        yield env.timeout(0)
        for number in range(1, 4):
            levels.append(int(level.integers(10, 20 + 1)))
            env.publish_event(
                f"readings-{number}",
                {"level": levels[-1]},
                task="reading",
                instance=number - 1,
            )

    def orders():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            last = levels[-3:]
            env.publish_event(
                f"orders-{number}",
                {"average": sum(last) / len(last)},
                task="order",
                instance=number - 1,
            )

    env.process(reading_arrivals())
    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 0.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'readings-1', 'task': 'reading', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'level': 18}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 0.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'readings-2', 'task': 'reading', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'level': 11}}
```

# row

`row`: one row of a CSV or Parquet file as a mapping, read once at load. A cell of digits is read as a number, so a postal code with leading zeros loses them; write them with `{gen: format, template: "{n:05d}"}`. `where` is an expression over the row's columns that keeps some rows; `weight` names a column of weights; `order` is `random` (the default), `sequential`, `shuffle` (every row once, in a random order) or `circular` (in file order, again from the first); `on_end` says what a `sequential` or `shuffle` order does when the rows run out: `error` (the default), `loop` or `stop`, which ends the run.

Use it for a whole row of a CSV or Parquet file, such as a product from a price list.

## Keys

| Key      | Type                                                | Default    |
| -------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `gen`    | `row`                                               | required   |
| `file`   | text                                                | required   |
| `where`  | text                                                | none       |
| `weight` | text                                                | none       |
| `order`  | `random` or `sequential` or `shuffle` or `circular` | `"random"` |
| `on_end` | `stop` or `loop` or `error`                         | `"error"`  |

Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

## Example

`product` is one row of `products.csv`, and `shuffle` gives every row once, in a random order. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Row: one row of a CSV file.
# An order starts every 60 seconds, and the run lasts 200 seconds, so three orders
# start. The file is `products.csv` in this folder.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/row.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  order:
    payload:
      product: {gen: row, file: products.csv, order: shuffle}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Row: one row of a CSV file, builder API.

The builder version of `row.yaml`. A builder script reads the file from the working
directory, so run it from the repository root.

Run it with: python examples/generators/row_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    payload = Template(
        {
            "product": {
                "gen": "row",
                "file": "examples/generators/products.csv",
                "order": "shuffle",
            }
        },
        name="tasks.order",
    )

    @app.task(name="order")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Row: one row of a CSV file, low-level API.

The low-level version of `row.yaml`: plain SimPy on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`,
which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each draw is made with
`Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's generator at that
place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The script reads the file from the working
directory, so run it from the repository root. A cell of digits is a number. `order:
shuffle` draws one permutation of the rows with `permutation(len(rows))` and gives the
rows in that order.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/row_low_level.py
"""

import csv
import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def _cell(text):
    """A cell of digits is a whole number, one with a point is a decimal number."""
    for kind in (int, float):
        try:
            return kind(text)
        except ValueError:
            pass
    return text


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    shuffle = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.product")
    with open("examples/generators/products.csv", newline="") as file:
        rows = [
            {name: _cell(text) for name, text in row.items()}
            for row in csv.DictReader(file)
        ]
    order = [int(i) for i in shuffle.permutation(len(rows))]

    def orders():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            payload = {"product": rows[order[number - 1]]}
            env.publish_event(
                f"orders-{number}", payload, task="order", instance=number - 1
            )

    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'product': {'sku': 'A-1', 'price': 2.5, 'weight': 1}}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'product': {'sku': 'C-3', 'price': 6, 'weight': 6}}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'product': {'sku': 'B-2', 'price': 4, 'weight': 3}}}
```

# call

`call`: what a `!python` function returns, called as `function(context, **kwargs)` with the kwargs evaluated first.

Use it for a value that your own Python function computes.

## Keys

| Key        | Type                      | Default  |
| ---------- | ------------------------- | -------- |
| `gen`      | `call`                    | required |
| `function` | !python reference         | required |
| `kwargs`   | mapping of names to Value |          |

A `Value` is a constant or a generator, as [What a Generator Is](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#what-a-generator-is) explains. Every kind also accepts `null_rate`, `unique`, `omit_rate` and `omit_when`, which [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/#keys-every-kind-accepts) describes.

## Example

`total` is a price from 10 to 50 plus a tax of 10 per cent, added by `with_tax` in `call_helpers.py`. An order starts every 60 seconds for 200 seconds, with the seed 42, so three orders start.

```yaml
# Call: what a Python function returns.
# An order starts every 60 seconds, and the run lasts 200 seconds, so three orders
# start. The function is in `call_helpers.py` in this folder.
#
# Run it with: desflow run examples/generators/call.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Gen
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  orders: {dist: constant, value: 60, spawn: order}

tasks:
  order:
    payload:
      total:
        gen: call
        function: !python call_helpers.with_tax
        kwargs:
          price: {gen: integer, bounds: [10, 50]}

run: {until: 200}
```

```python
"""Call: what a Python function returns, builder API.

The builder version of `call.yaml`. The function is passed as it is, where a blueprint
names it with `!python`.

Run it with: python examples/generators/call_builder.py
"""

import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from call_helpers import with_tax

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, SimulationContext
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 200


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the model."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Gen",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(ConsoleEgress())
    app.add_arrival("orders", "constant", value=60, spawn="order")
    payload = Template(
        {
            "total": {
                "gen": "call",
                "function": with_tax,
                "kwargs": {"price": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [10, 50]}},
            }
        },
        name="tasks.order",
    )

    @app.task(name="order")
    def order(task_id):
        """Gives one order."""
        return payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

```python
"""Call: what a Python function returns, low-level API.

The low-level version of `call.yaml`: plain SimPy on a `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`,
which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each draw is made with
`Sampler.generator(<place>)`, the random sequence of the blueprint's generator at that
place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The function is the one a blueprint names with
`!python`. It gets no context, because the script has none and passes None.

Needs: nothing.
Run it with: python examples/generators/call_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from call_helpers import with_tax

from desflow import ConsoleEgress, DynamicRealtimeEnvironment, Sampler

UNTIL = 200
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the processes on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    price = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.total.kwargs.price")

    def orders():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(60)
            total = with_tax(None, int(price.integers(10, 50 + 1)))
            env.publish_event(
                f"orders-{number}", {"total": total}, task="order", instance=number - 1
            )

    env.process(orders())


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced into the console."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    env.setup_egress([ConsoleEgress()])
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

All three print the same records:

```text
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 60.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-1', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 0, 'value': {'total': 35.2}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 120.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-2', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 1, 'value': {'total': 55.0}}
[EVT] {'sim_ts': 180.0, 'timestamp': '...', 'key': 'orders-3', 'task': 'order', 'instance': 2, 'value': {'total': 49.5}}
```

# Gallery

The Gallery holds end-to-end examples. Each is a complete file that you can run, and each is written three ways: as a YAML blueprint, with the builder API and with the low-level API. Its page shows the three versions in tabs. [Ways to write a simulation](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/index.md) compares the three.

## Data Generation

Blueprints that generate data for a table, a stream or a test. They run unpaced and need no service unless the page says so.

| Page                                                                                                               | What it covers                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Data Sets](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/data-generation/data-sets/index.md)                         | a retail set written to three sinks, a film rental store, auction streams, a group-by table, taxi rides, labelled text and a point-in-time training set                         |
| [Event Streams](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/data-generation/event-streams/index.md)                 | orders that carry their customer's tier, a stolen card that makes three large payments, stock queries, traces of nested spans and customer deletes that become Kafka tombstones |
| [Processes with Queues](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/data-generation/processes-with-queues/index.md) | busy packers, a machine that wears, a falling capacity, callers who hang up, urgent tickets, shopping carts, a sign-up funnel, bets and audits                                  |

## Simulation Models

Complete models that read from or write to a service, or that run unpaced to files.

| Example                                                                                                            | What it covers                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Local Simulation](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/local/index.md)                    | prints events and telemetry, with no container                             |
| [Kafka Digital Twin](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/kafka/index.md)                  | takes updates from Kafka and publishes events and telemetry to Kafka       |
| [Fast-Forward to Parquet](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/parquet/index.md)           | data generated unpaced at `factor=0.0`: a week written to Parquet          |
| [Fast-Forward to Iceberg](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/iceberg/index.md)           | data generated unpaced at `factor=0.0`: a day appended to an Iceberg table |
| [PostgreSQL](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/postgres/index.md)                       | writes orders to PostgreSQL and takes updates from a table                 |
| [Redis](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/redis/index.md)                               | writes to a Redis Stream and takes updates from Pub/Sub                    |
| [Parquet History, Kafka Live](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/backfill-live/index.md) | backdated history to Parquet, then live to Kafka                           |
| [Related Records](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/simulation-models/advanced-postgres-orders/index.md)  | orders and their line items, in two PostgreSQL tables                      |

## More Examples

[Projects Using desflow](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/projects/index.md) lists public projects that generate their data with desflow. The seven programs of SimPy's own documentation, each written in desflow, are in [SimPy Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/examples/index.md).

Each example page says how to download and run it, and which odctl profile from [Services for the Examples](#services-for-the-examples) it needs. `desflow examples get` prints the extra an example needs, and `pip install "desflow[all]"` installs every extra, so each example runs once its profile is up.

`desflow examples list` prints every example in the terminal, with the odctl profile each one needs. The list also has the shop examples, such as `stock` and `breakdowns`, which are shown on the page that teaches their feature. `desflow examples get NAME` downloads the files of the release you installed into `NAME/yaml/`, `NAME/builder/` and `NAME/low-level/`. `--api` keeps one version, `--dest` downloads into another folder, `--ref` names another tag or branch, such as `main`, and `--force` replaces files that are already there:

```bash
desflow examples list
desflow examples get local --api yaml --dest work
```

The second command writes `work/local/yaml/local.yaml`.

______________________________________________________________________

## Services for the Examples

Every example that needs a broker, a database or an object store gets it from [odctl](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl), a separate CLI that manages curated Docker Compose stacks. Install it once:

```bash
# With uv
uv tool install "odctl>=1.0,<2"

# Or with pip
pip install "odctl>=1.0,<2"
```

`odctl list -d` shows every profile and the ports it publishes. The examples here use five of them: `kafka-lite`, `postgres`, `valkey`, `storage` and `catalog`.

### Starting a Profile

Each example needs at most one odctl profile. Start the profile before you run the example, and stop it afterwards:

| Example                                                                                      | Start                 | Stop                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| every example that `desflow examples` marks `(no service)`, such as local, parquet and stock | nothing needed        |                                   |
| kafka, backfill-live                                                                         | `odctl up kafka-lite` | `odctl down kafka-lite --volumes` |
| postgres, related-records                                                                    | `odctl up postgres`   | `odctl down postgres --volumes`   |
| redis                                                                                        | `odctl up valkey`     | `odctl down valkey --volumes`     |
| parquet with `PARQUET_FILESYSTEM=s3`                                                         | `odctl up storage`    | `odctl down storage --volumes`    |
| iceberg                                                                                      | `odctl up catalog`    | `odctl down catalog --volumes`    |

An example's YAML version needs the same profile as its builder version: `desflow examples get <name>` prints the profile with the run command.

The Kafka and Redis profiles are not named after their service. odctl's one-broker Kafka profile is `kafka-lite` and its three-broker Kafka profile is `kafka-full`. odctl runs Valkey in place of Redis, so its Redis profile is `valkey`. The Kafka examples run on either Kafka profile, because both publish a broker at `127.0.0.1:9092`.

### Endpoints These Profiles Publish

These are the addresses the examples use. Every profile publishes on your machine only, on `127.0.0.1`. Use that address rather than `localhost`, which macOS resolves to the IPv6 address `::1` first, where nothing listens.

| Profile      | Service                                              | Address the examples use                                                                |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kafka-lite` | Kafka, one broker, with the Karapace schema registry | `127.0.0.1:9092`; schema registry `http://127.0.0.1:8081`                               |
| `kafka-full` | Kafka, three brokers, with the same schema registry  | `127.0.0.1:9092,127.0.0.1:9093,127.0.0.1:9094`; schema registry `http://127.0.0.1:8081` |
| `postgres`   | PostgreSQL, database `odctl`                         | `postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/odctl`                                       |
| `valkey`     | Valkey (Redis protocol)                              | `redis://user:password@127.0.0.1:6379/0`                                                |
| `storage`    | S3-compatible object store, bucket `odctl-dev`       | `http://127.0.0.1:8333`, access key `user`, secret key `password`                       |
| `catalog`    | Iceberg REST catalog, warehouse `s3://warehouse/`    | `http://127.0.0.1:8181`                                                                 |

`odctl list -d` shows every port a profile publishes.

# Data Sets

Seven data sets, each generated by one blueprint: a retail set written to three sinks, a film rental store, auction streams, a group-by table, taxi rides, labelled text and a point-in-time training set. Each entry is a complete file in three forms, so you can run it, read how it is built and change it.

______________________________________________________________________

## Before You Start

The commands run from the root of a clone of the repository, where the files are in `examples/gallery/`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow.git
cd desflow
```

An entry that needs a service or an extra says so. [Services for the Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/#services-for-the-examples) shows how to start the services. A file with a fixed `random_seed` and `factor: 0` prints the same records on every run, and each output block below holds the first events of the YAML file. The Builder and Low-level files publish the same records.

______________________________________________________________________

## Entries

### Retail records go to PostgreSQL, Kafka and Parquet

A shop has 20 customers and 10 products at the start and takes about one order every two seconds. Each order picks a customer and a product at random and is followed by its invoice. The reference data goes to PostgreSQL tables, the orders to a Kafka topic and the invoices to a Parquet file, each sink taking the records of its own tasks (the `when` expression of the entry).

It needs a broker and a database, started with `odctl up kafka-lite` and `odctl up postgres`, and the `kafka`, `postgres`, `parquet` and `fake` extras. `KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS` sets the broker address and `DEST_PATH` the folder of the Parquet file (`data` by default), so this entry shows no output block here.

Run it with the sample option, which stops after the first events and prints them:

```bash
desflow run examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks.yaml --sample 5
```

```yaml
# Retail records go to PostgreSQL, Kafka and Parquet.
#
# A shop has 20 customers and 10 products at the start and takes about one order every
# two seconds. Each order picks a customer and a product at random and is followed by
# its invoice. The reference data goes to PostgreSQL tables, the orders to a Kafka
# topic and the invoices to a Parquet file, each sink taking the records of its own
# tasks (the `when` expression of the entry).
#
# Needs: a broker and a database, with odctl up kafka-lite and odctl up postgres, and
# the kafka, postgres, parquet and fake extras. KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS sets the broker
# address, and DEST_PATH the folder of the Parquet file (data by default).
# Run it with: desflow run examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Retail
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - type: Postgres
    when: {expr: "record.task == 'customer'"}
    config:
      connection_dsn: postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/odctl
      tables:
        customers:
          columns: {customer_id: INT, name: TEXT, country: TEXT}
          primary_key: customer_id
  - type: Postgres
    when: {expr: "record.task == 'product'"}
    config:
      connection_dsn: postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/odctl
      tables:
        products:
          columns: {product_id: INT, title: TEXT, price: REAL}
          primary_key: product_id
  - type: Kafka
    when: {expr: "record.task == 'order'"}
    config:
      bootstrap_servers: ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS:-localhost:9092}
      event_topic: retail-orders
  - type: Parquet
    when: {expr: "record.task == 'invoice'"}
    config: {default_path: "${DEST_PATH:-data}/invoices.parquet"}

arrivals:
  customers: {initial: 20, spawn: customer}
  products: {initial: 10, spawn: product}
  orders: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.5, spawn: order}

tasks:
  customer:
    payload:
      customer_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      name: {gen: fake, method: name}
      country:
        gen: weighted
        options: {AU: 5, US: 3, GB: 2}

  product:
    payload:
      product_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      title:
        gen: one_of
        choices: [Desk lamp, Notebook, Water bottle, Backpack, Headphones, Keyboard]
      price: {gen: uniform, low: 2, high: 200, decimals: 2}

  order:
    vars:
      product: {gen: lookup, task: product}
      price: {gen: var, name: product, path: price}
      quantity: {gen: integer, bounds: [1, 5]}
    payload:
      order_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      customer_id: {gen: lookup, task: customer, path: customer_id}
      product_id: {gen: var, name: product, path: product_id}
      quantity: {gen: var, name: quantity}
      total: {gen: expr, expr: "round(price * quantity, 2)"}
    next: invoice

  invoice:
    payload:
      order_id: {gen: upstream, path: order_id}
      amount: {gen: upstream, path: total}

run: {until: 10 min}
```

The Builder file builds the same model with the builder API and prints every record of its run:

```bash
python examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks_builder.py
```

```python
"""Retail records go to PostgreSQL, Kafka and Parquet, builder API.

The builder version of `retail_records_to_three_sinks.yaml`: 20 customers and 10
products at the start, an order about every two seconds and an invoice for each order.
The customers and products go to PostgreSQL tables, the orders to a Kafka topic and the
invoices to a Parquet file.

Needs: a broker and a database, with odctl up kafka-lite and odctl up postgres, and the
kafka, postgres, parquet and fake extras. KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS sets the broker
address, and DEST_PATH the folder of the Parquet file (data by default).
Run it with: python examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks_builder.py
"""

import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from desflow import (
    KafkaEgress,
    ParquetStorageEgress,
    PostgresEgress,
    SimulationContext,
)
from desflow.values import Template

UNTIL = 600
DSN = "postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/odctl"


def build() -> SimulationContext:
    """Builds the shop, with a sink for each kind of record."""
    app = SimulationContext(
        sim_id="Retail",
        factor=0,
        random_seed=42,
        logical_start_time=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc),
    )
    app.add_egress(
        PostgresEgress(
            DSN,
            tables={
                "customers": {
                    "columns": {
                        "customer_id": "INT",
                        "name": "TEXT",
                        "country": "TEXT",
                    },
                    "primary_key": "customer_id",
                }
            },
        ),
        when=lambda record: record.get("task") == "customer",
    )
    app.add_egress(
        PostgresEgress(
            DSN,
            tables={
                "products": {
                    "columns": {"product_id": "INT", "title": "TEXT", "price": "REAL"},
                    "primary_key": "product_id",
                }
            },
        ),
        when=lambda record: record.get("task") == "product",
    )
    app.add_egress(
        KafkaEgress(
            bootstrap_servers=os.environ.get(
                "KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "localhost:9092"
            ),
            event_topic="retail-orders",
        ),
        when=lambda record: record.get("task") == "order",
    )
    app.add_egress(
        ParquetStorageEgress(
            default_path=f"{os.environ.get('DEST_PATH', 'data')}/invoices.parquet"
        ),
        when=lambda record: record.get("task") == "invoice",
    )
    app.add_initial_arrival("customers", 20, spawn="customer")
    app.add_initial_arrival("products", 10, spawn="product")
    app.add_arrival("orders", "exponential", rate=0.5, spawn="order")
    customer_payload = Template(
        {
            "customer_id": {"gen": "sequence", "start": 1},
            "name": {"gen": "fake", "method": "name"},
            "country": {"gen": "weighted", "options": {"AU": 5, "US": 3, "GB": 2}},
        },
        name="tasks.customer",
    )
    product_payload = Template(
        {
            "product_id": {"gen": "sequence", "start": 1},
            "title": {
                "gen": "one_of",
                "choices": [
                    "Desk lamp",
                    "Notebook",
                    "Water bottle",
                    "Backpack",
                    "Headphones",
                    "Keyboard",
                ],
            },
            "price": {"gen": "uniform", "low": 2, "high": 200, "decimals": 2},
        },
        name="tasks.product",
    )
    order_payload = Template(
        {
            "order_id": {"gen": "sequence", "start": 1},
            "customer_id": {"gen": "lookup", "task": "customer", "path": "customer_id"},
            "product_id": {"gen": "var", "name": "product", "path": "product_id"},
            "quantity": {"gen": "var", "name": "quantity"},
            "total": {"gen": "expr", "expr": "round(price * quantity, 2)"},
        },
        name="tasks.order",
        vars={
            "product": {"gen": "lookup", "task": "product"},
            "price": {"gen": "var", "name": "product", "path": "price"},
            "quantity": {"gen": "integer", "bounds": [1, 5]},
        },
    )
    invoice_payload = Template(
        {
            "order_id": {"gen": "upstream", "path": "order_id"},
            "amount": {"gen": "upstream", "path": "total"},
        },
        name="tasks.invoice",
    )

    @app.task(name="customer", history=1_000_000)
    def customer(task_id):
        """Gives one customer."""
        return customer_payload

    @app.task(name="product", history=1_000_000)
    def product(task_id):
        """Gives one product."""
        return product_payload

    @app.task(name="order", next="invoice")
    def order(task_id):
        """Takes one order."""
        return order_payload

    @app.task(name="invoice")
    def invoice(task_id):
        """Bills the order."""
        return invoice_payload

    return app


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    build().run(until=UNTIL)
```

The Low-level file builds the model on `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`, with plain Python processes, and prints every record of its run:

```bash
python examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks_low_level.py
```

The Low-level file draws each value with `Sampler.generator(<place>)`, where the place is the key path of the blueprint's generator that makes the same value, such as `tasks.customer.payload.name`, `tasks.customer.payload.country` and `tasks.product.payload.title` and 4 more. Each draw therefore comes from the random sequence the blueprint uses at the same place, so the draws are the blueprint's. The gaps between arrivals come from `Sampler.sample` on a `DistributionConfig` whose `stream` is `arrival.orders`, the sequence the blueprint uses for its arrivals.

```python
"""Retail records go to PostgreSQL, Kafka and Parquet, low-level API.

The low-level version of `retail_records_to_three_sinks.yaml`: plain SimPy on a
`DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`, which publishes each record with `publish_event`. Each
draw is made with `Sampler.generator(<name>)`, from the random sequence the blueprint's
generator at that place uses, so the draws are the blueprint's. A name is drawn with a
Faker that is seeded from that sequence.

Needs: a broker and a database, with odctl up kafka-lite and odctl up postgres, and the
kafka, postgres, parquet and fake extras. KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS sets the broker
address, and DEST_PATH the folder of the Parquet file (data by default).
Run it with: python examples/gallery/retail_records_to_three_sinks_low_level.py
"""

import itertools
import logging
import os
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from faker import Faker

from desflow import (
    DistributionConfig,
    DynamicRealtimeEnvironment,
    KafkaEgress,
    ParquetStorageEgress,
    PostgresEgress,
    Sampler,
)

UNTIL = 600
START = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
ENVIRONMENT = {"logical_start_time": START, "timezone": "UTC"}
DSN = "postgresql://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/odctl"
COUNTRIES = {"AU": 5, "US": 3, "GB": 2}
TITLES = ["Desk lamp", "Notebook", "Water bottle", "Backpack", "Headphones", "Keyboard"]


def weighted(rng, options):
    """One key of `options`, chosen by its weight, as the `weighted` generator does."""
    point = rng.random() * sum(options.values())
    running = 0.0
    for value, weight in options.items():
        running += weight
        if point < running:
            return value
    return value


def build(env: DynamicRealtimeEnvironment) -> None:
    """Starts the arrivals on `env`."""
    sampler = Sampler(seed=42)
    faker = Faker("en_US")
    faker.seed_instance(
        int(sampler.generator("tasks.customer.payload.name#fake").integers(2**32))
    )
    country = sampler.generator("tasks.customer.payload.country")
    title = sampler.generator("tasks.product.payload.title")
    price = sampler.generator("tasks.product.payload.price")
    product_row = sampler.generator("tasks.order.vars.product")
    quantity = sampler.generator("tasks.order.vars.quantity")
    customer_row = sampler.generator("tasks.order.payload.customer_id")
    customers: list = []  # the ids of the customers so far, oldest first
    products: list = []  # the products so far, oldest first
    counts = {"customer": 0, "product": 0, "order": 0, "invoice": 0}

    def publish(key, task, payload):
        """Publishes a finished payload as the next instance of its task."""
        env.publish_event(key, payload, task=task, instance=counts[task])
        counts[task] += 1

    def customer():
        row = {
            "customer_id": len(customers) + 1,
            "name": faker.name(),
            "country": weighted(country, COUNTRIES),
        }
        customers.append(row["customer_id"])
        return row

    def product():
        row = {
            "product_id": len(products) + 1,
            "title": TITLES[int(title.integers(len(TITLES)))],
            "price": round(2 + (200 - 2) * price.random(), 2),
        }
        products.append(row)
        return row

    def order(number):
        """An order, and the invoice for it at once."""
        key = f"orders-{number}"
        chosen = products[int(product_row.integers(len(products)))]
        count = int(quantity.integers(1, 6))
        taken = {
            "order_id": number,
            "customer_id": customers[int(customer_row.integers(len(customers)))],
            "product_id": chosen["product_id"],
            "quantity": count,
            "total": round(chosen["price"] * count, 2),
        }
        publish(key, "order", taken)
        publish(key, "invoice", {"order_id": number, "amount": taken["total"]})

    gap = DistributionConfig(dist="exponential", rate=0.5)
    gap.stream = "arrival.orders"

    def source():
        for number in itertools.count(1):
            yield env.timeout(sampler.sample(gap))
            order(number)

    def start(name, task, make, number):
        yield env.timeout(0)
        publish(f"{name}-{number}", task, make())

    env.process(source())
    for number in range(1, 21):
        env.process(start("customers", "customer", customer, number))
    for number in range(1, 11):
        env.process(start("products", "product", product, number))


def run() -> None:
    """Runs the model unpaced, with a sink for each kind of record."""
    env = DynamicRealtimeEnvironment(factor=0, **ENVIRONMENT)
    bootstrap = os.environ.get("KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS", "localhost:9092")
    sinks = [
        (
            PostgresEgress(
                DSN,
                tables={
                    "customers": {
                        "columns": {
                            "customer_id": "INT",
                            "name": "TEXT",
                            "country": "TEXT",
                        },
                        "primary_key": "customer_id",
                    }
                },
            ),
            "customer",
        ),
        (
            PostgresEgress(
                DSN,
                tables={
                    "products": {
                        "columns": {
                            "product_id": "INT",
                            "title": "TEXT",
                            "price": "REAL",
                        },
                        "primary_key": "product_id",
                    }
                },
            ),
            "product",
        ),
        (
            KafkaEgress(bootstrap_servers=bootstrap, event_topic="retail-orders"),
            "order",
        ),
        (
            ParquetStorageEgress(
                default_path=f"{os.environ.get('DEST_PATH', 'data')}/invoices.parquet"
            ),
            "invoice",
        ),
    ]
    env.setup_egress(
        [sink for sink, _ in sinks],
        predicates=[
            lambda record, task=task: record.get("task") == task for _, task in sinks
        ],
    )
    build(env)
    try:
        env.run(until=UNTIL)
    finally:
        env.teardown()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")
    run()
```

### A film rental store: films, customers, rentals, payments and returns

The tables have the shape of the Sakila sample database. A store has 20 films and 15 customers at the start. About one rental starts every 8 minutes, for a week. A rental names a film and a customer that exist, is paid for at once at the film's rental rate, and is returned 1 to 7 days later.

It needs the `fake` extra: `pip install "desflow[fake]"`.

Run it with the sample option, which stops after the first events and prints them:

```bash
desflow run examples/gallery/film_rental_store.yaml --sample 5
```

```yaml
# A film rental store: films, customers, rentals, payments and returns.
#
# The tables have the shape of the Sakila sample database. A store has 20 films and 15
# customers at the start. About one rental starts every 8 minutes, for a week. A rental
# names a film and a customer that exist, is paid for at once at the film's rental rate,
# and is returned 1 to 7 days later.
#
# Needs: the fake extra.
# Run it with: desflow run examples/gallery/film_rental_store.yaml

simulation:
  sim_id: Store
  factor: 0
  random_seed: 42
  logical_start_time: 2026-01-01T00:00:00

egress:
  - {type: Console}

arrivals:
  films: {initial: 20, spawn: film}
  customers: {initial: 15, spawn: customer}
  rentals: {dist: exponential, rate: 0.002, spawn: rental}

tasks:
  film:
    payload:
      film_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      title:
        gen: format
        template: "{adjective} {noun}"
        names:
          adjective: {gen: one_of, choices: [Silent, Broken, Golden, Hidden, Last]}
          noun: {gen: one_of, choices: [River, Garden, Highway, Letter, Harbour]}
      rating:
        gen: weighted
        options: {G: 2, PG: 3, PG-13: 3, R: 3, NC-17: 1}
      rental_rate: {gen: one_of, choices: [0.99, 2.99, 4.99]}
      length: {gen: integer, bounds: [60, 180]}

  customer:
    payload:
      customer_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      first_name: {gen: fake, method: first_name}
      last_name: {gen: fake, method: last_name}
      active: {gen: boolean, p: 0.9}

  rental:
    vars:
      film: {gen: lookup, task: film}
    payload:
      rental_id: {gen: sequence, start: 1}
      rental_date: {gen: now}
      film_id: {gen: var, name: film, path: film_id}
      rental_rate: {gen: var, name: film, path: rental_rate}
      customer_id: {gen: lookup, task: customer, path: customer_id}
    next: payment

  payment:
    payload:
      rental_id: {gen: upstream, path: rental_id}
      customer_id: {gen: upstream, path: customer_id}
      amount: {gen: upstream, path: rental_rate}
      payment_date: {gen: now}
    next: return

  return:
    # 1 to 7 days, in seconds
    wait:
      timeout: {gen: uniform, low: 86400, high: 604800}
    payload:
      rental_id: {gen: upstream, path: rental_id}
      return_date: {gen: now}

run: {until: 7 days}
```

The Builder file builds the same model with the builder API and prints every record of its run:

```bash
python examples/gallery/film_rental_store_builder.py
```
