A label goes to `event_topic` with no key                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `RedisEgress`                                                        | the record as JSON in one `payload` field, with any `__stream__` key removed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `ParquetStorageEgress`, `JsonlStorageEgress`, `IcebergStorageEgress` | without a router, one flat row per event or label, with an event's `value` mapping unpacked into columns, and no telemetry; with a router, each record as the router leaves it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `PostgresEgress`                                                     | an event or telemetry record whose value is a mapping, written to the table its `__table__` key names; the key is removed. The sink adds `sim_ts` and `timestamp` to the row, and for an event `key` as `event_id`, `task` and `instance`, or for telemetry `path_id`, as [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#postgresql) describes. A label is written as the columns `sim_ts`, `timestamp`, `path`, `old`, `new` and `label`, the last three as JSON text |

With `envelope: false` on the entry, a sink writes each event's `value` alone: no `stream_type`, `sim_ts`, `timestamp`, `key`, `task` or `instance`, and no telemetry and no `queued` or `started` record of a task. A label record of a `when: labels` entry is left whole. A Kafka sink sends a null value as a tombstone, a message with the record's key and a null value, and a value that is not a mapping as JSON. A Redis sink sends a value that is not a mapping as JSON. A file, Iceberg or PostgreSQL sink skips such a value with one warning. [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#write-the-value-alone) shows the key. 1.x keeps this shape.

In a flat row, a finished event's columns are its task's payload only. The `queued` and `started` rows of a task carry `path_id`, `sim_id`, `service` and `status`. Its finished row has them null unless the payload holds them. [Egress](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#parquet-and-json-lines) describes the file sinks.
# About

# Why desflow

I like building demo apps, and every demo app needs data. I could not find enough public APIs that suited my projects, and the fake data scripts I wrote did not work well: each app needed its own, and none of them behaved like a real system.

Then I came across discrete-event simulation (DES). A DES models the process itself: what arrives, which resources serve it and how long each step takes. The data follows from that model, so it has cause and effect, as a real system does. For example, a queue grows because orders arrive faster than packers can handle them. A few numbers, such as an arrival rate, a capacity and a service time, are enough for queues, waits and backlogs that change over time. A simulation also runs much faster than real time, and the same seed gives the same data every time.

[SimPy](https://simpy.readthedocs.io/) is the standard DES library for Python, but it could not do two things I needed: change the parameters of a simulation while it runs, and write the events to external systems. So I started this project, under the name dynamic-des, to add both.

Later I found that a SimPy model needs a lot of code around it: the environment, the resources, the generators and the record of what happened, all written by hand. I had used the builder pattern in PySpark, so I applied it here and added a builder in Python. Not everyone is a Python programmer, though, so I also added a YAML format, an idea I took from Apache Beam YAML.

Next I looked for ways to manage and schedule simulations from a server, an idea inspired by Airflow, and changed the name to desflow.

From here, I want a simulation to be easier to create, whether it is written by hand, by an AI assistant, or built from the history of a real system. I also want desflow to fit into the tools people already use. Creating a simulation is only the first step: its value is in analysing and testing with it. The server is where these come together, as one place to create, analyse, test, monitor and manage simulations, for people and for AI agents. The [Roadmap](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/roadmap/index.md) lists the plans.

When I learned DES, what I needed was spread across textbooks, lecture notes and papers. So I added a [Learn](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/what-is-des/index.md) section that brings it together in one place and teaches DES itself, not only desflow, with code you can run. It is for anyone who is new to DES, whether or not they use desflow. The [`desflow` command](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/index.md) supports this learning too: the Learn pages use its `explain` command to check a model against queueing theory.

If you already model with SimPy, desflow keeps what you know: a desflow model is SimPy underneath, with the additions above, and it covers everything a SimPy model can do. [Coming from SimPy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/coming-from-simpy/index.md) shows where each part of a SimPy model goes.

I use desflow in my own projects, such as the demos in [benchtop](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/benchtop). It is useful in many kinds of project. A few examples:

- **Simulation studies.** A question such as how many packers a shop needs takes many runs of a model. In SimPy you write the replications, the statistics and the confidence intervals yourself. desflow collects the statistics, runs the [replications](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/replications/index.md) and compares [designs](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/experiments/index.md) from one command, and `desflow explain` names the bottleneck before anything runs. See [Queues and Capacity](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/first-model/queues-and-capacity/index.md) for the full worked example.
- **Data engineering.** Batch and streaming pipelines need data that moves like a real system. desflow writes it to Kafka, Redis, PostgreSQL, Parquet and JSONL files, and Iceberg tables, as history at full speed and then live.
- **ML and MLOps.** A model that predicts delays or load needs training data in which queues build and clear for a reason. When a parameter changes during a run, the data shifts at a known time, which is what a drift monitor has to catch.
- **AI.** An anomaly detector or an AI agent needs a known answer to be scored against. A seeded run can plant a fault and record what it planted as label records.

# Roadmap

Releases come in the order shown, without dates: a release ships when it is ready. Each item links to its GitHub issue.

## Before 1.0

1.0.0: Stable

1.0.0 sets the version number and the Production/Stable classifier, with only the fixes of the two weeks of checks. From here the format, the command, the public API and the record format stay compatible across 1.x, as the [Compatibility Policy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/compatibility/index.md) sets out. [#54](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/54)

## What 1.0 means

From 1.0, the YAML blueprint format, the `desflow` command, the public Python API and the published record format stay compatible across every 1.x release. The public Python API is the set of promised import paths, which the [Compatibility Policy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/compatibility/index.md) lists. The package status moves from Beta to Production/Stable. The names kept for compatibility, `dynamic_des`, `ddes` and the old registry settings, are removed in 1.0, and [Upgrading to 1.0](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/upgrading-to-1.0/#removed-names) lists each.

## After 1.0

### From history to simulation

- **Model discovery:** a model discovered from an event log.
- **Comparison with the log:** a run compared with the log.
- **A model kept current:** the model updated from new logs.

### Simulation model

- **Maintenance, schedules and incidents:** planned maintenance, schedules that repeat by time of day, and incidents that change several parameters at once. 0.22.0 ships random breakdowns with repair and finite schedules, and 1.0 ships a failure clock that runs only while a resource works (`clock: busy`).
- **More flow and resource features:** matching and splitting, setup times, and resources chosen by skill. 1.0 ships batching.
- **Costs and continuous flow:** costs and energy per resource state, and levels that rise and fall continuously.
- **Transport on maps:** vehicles that move between locations on real roads and publish their positions.
- **Data-driven inputs:** arrivals replayed from a database, or taken live from a Kafka topic.
- **Models read from a store:** a value that a model reads from a store during a run, such as the trained model of a recommender, with a key of its own. In 1.0 this is a `!python` function, as [Call Python from YAML](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/tools/yaml-advanced/index.md) shows.
- **Decisions from outside:** a dispatcher or an agent answers for one order or session, and a run can repeat exactly from a log of those answers.

### Analysis

- **Experiments:** experiment designs, optimisation, and calibration against observed data.
- **Fitting and comparison:** distribution fitting from more data sources, automatic fault-impact experiments, and fuller run comparison and fidelity scoring.

### Simulation server

The server ships after 1.0, as 1.x releases installed with the `server` extra.

- **Server API and MCP tools:** `desflow serve` runs simulations through a REST API: upload, start, stop, change parameters during a run and follow its events. MCP tools, which let an AI agent do the same, are experimental. ([#48](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/48))
- **Browser UI:** the same from a browser, including each simulation's graph from `desflow explain`. ([#49](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/49))
- **Schedules:** run simulations on cron schedules. ([#50](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/50))
- **Server image and odctl profile:** a published image and an [odctl](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl) profile run the server locally with nothing installed on the host. ([#52](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/52))
- **Visualisation:** a graph image from `desflow explain`, animation of a running or recorded simulation, and a map view.
- **Distributed runs:** workers on several machines.

### Writing simulations

- **Payloads from your data:** record fields generated from a schema or a few sample records, so the records have the real field names, types and value ranges.
- **Visual builder.**
- **Conversion:** turn a YAML blueprint into builder code, and builder code into YAML with no Python, with an error that names each part that cannot be converted and how to rewrite it.

### Connectors

- **More sinks:** a webhook sink, a generic SQL sink and more.
- **Error sink:** records a sink could not write go to another sink instead of being lost, and a run can fail when too many do.
- **Delivery faults:** records delivered late, twice, damaged or not at all, to test how a pipeline handles them.
- **Lineage:** each run reported to OpenLineage and OpenMetadata.

### Integrations

- **Orchestrators:** Airflow, Dagster and similar tools.
- **AI assistants:** the Claude Code plugin and its marketplace.
- **Testing tools:** a pytest plugin and a GitHub Action.
- **Query engines and streaming databases.**
- **Data quality and evaluation tools.**

### Platform

- **More speed:** cheaper record publishing, which takes about 40 percent of a run's time, with the same published records ([#69](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/69)), and a faster runtime for YAML-only blueprints if measurements show the need.

## Released

1.0.0rc3: The last candidate

- **Fixes from the checks:** an interrupt with `on_interrupt: resume`, or a batch closing, at the instant a task's patience ran out no longer stops the run. A YAML file and the Builder refuse a name a place cannot read, and a batch size of `true`, with one text, and a refusal names the first unknown name in sorted order on every run. No format, command or record changes. [#54](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/54)
- **Docs:** SimPy Compatibility says where desflow differs in a detail for a native feature, YAML Keys says what `Value` and `Generator` mean, and Upgrading to 1.0 lists the new logger names.

1.0.0rc2: A cleaner internal structure

- **Reorganised code:** the packages sit in layers that an import contract checks, the code that declares and runs a model moves to its own package, and the largest classes are split by their groups, with no change of behaviour. No format, command or record changes. [#54](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/54)
- **How desflow Works:** diagrams of the core, builder and blueprint packages, and one task instance's steps on Tasks and Processes.

1.0.0rc1: What 1.0 brings

- **SimPy's rules:** a run ends when no event is left, as in SimPy, and `strict` and `on_unhandled_failure` default to SimPy's values. The SimPy Compatibility page shows each SimPy feature in YAML, Builder and Low-level with its status.
- **SimPy's step order at a tie:** a task with one `wait` branch, the task after `next`, the actions of `on:` and a resumed job go on in the same simulation step as SimPy's process, so records at one instant can change order. [#105](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/105)
- **YAML with no Python:** every known case runs in YAML alone, with `--var`, `--watch`, generated values, `desflow check` and `desflow test`.
- **SimPy's examples:** the seven examples of SimPy's docs in YAML, Builder and Low-level. [#95](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/95)
- **Record contract frozen:** the records 1.x keeps. [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)
- **Old names removed:** `dynamic_des`, `ddes` and the other names kept for compatibility. [#84](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/84)
- **Pydantic 2.6.1 or later.** [#104](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/104)
- **Rewritten docs.** Each change that alters records is listed under Upgrading to 1.0.

0.28.0: Library hooks for the server

- **Parameter changes that report back:** `change` returns a `ParamChange` or raises `ParamRejected`, `on_change` callbacks receive every accepted change with its source, and `registry_paths()` lists the paths a simulation will have without running it. [#70](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/70)
- **File ingress:** `FileIngress` changes parameters during a run when you edit a local file, with no broker. [#86](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/86)
- **Scenario values checked:** a scenario step whose value the registry refuses stops the load or the start, instead of being logged and ignored. [#93](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/93)
- **Drafting from a description:** the AI skill teaches an assistant to draft a model from a description of a process. [#94](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/94)

0.27.0: Schema registry formats

- **JSON Schema and Protobuf:** serializers and deserializers for both formats, through the Confluent and Glue schema registries, next to Avro. [#82](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/82)
- **Glue wire format:** desflow writes and reads it itself, so the `glue` extra no longer installs aws-glue-schema-registry.
- **Kafka:** the `kafka` extra no longer installs kafka-python, and topics are created through aiokafka.

0.26.0: Storage, schema registry code and Python 3.15

- **Storage:** Parquet and JSON Lines files on Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob Storage, and Iceberg tables through SQL catalogs on SQLite or PostgreSQL and the Glue catalog. [#32](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/32)
- **Schema registry code:** the Confluent schema registry client moves into desflow, so the `confluent` extra no longer installs confluent-kafka. [#83](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/83)
- **Python 3.15** is supported. [#40](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/40)
- **Fix:** `GlueAvroSerializer` serializes a record. [#85](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/85)
- **Docs:** page addresses follow the sidebar, and each page kind has one shape.

0.25.0: desflow explain

- **desflow explain:** `desflow explain` shows a simulation as a graph, marks each resource OK, congested or unstable (its queue grows without limit), names the bottleneck and suggests changes. [#47](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/47)
- **Commands:** `desflow dist` converts between a distribution's parameters and its mean and standard deviation. `desflow run --sample` prints a few records from a blueprint, and `--stdout` sends every record except the `system.simulation.lag_seconds` readings to the standard output as JSON lines in place of the real sinks.
- **Library:** `load_context` loads a simulation folder from Python. Builder arrivals can name the task they start.
- **Docs:** a generated reference page for the `desflow` command, and in Learn, Complete Model, the `explain` section of Checking a Model and Check Against Theory. [#60](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/60)

0.24.0: Blueprint schema and AI skill

- **Blueprint schema and AI skill:** a JSON Schema for blueprints, shipped in the package and on the docs site, so editors complete keys and flag mistakes as you type, with a YAML Keys reference page generated from it. A skill that teaches an AI assistant to write and check blueprints. [#41](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/41)
- **Public API test:** a test that fails when a public name or signature of the library or the `desflow` command is removed or changed. [#67](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/67)
- **Removal:** `resource.queue.items`, which warns since 0.23.0, is removed: use `list(resource.queue)`.
- **Learn section:** the concept pages, Checking a Model, Live Changes, Streaming Out and the How-To pages that do not need `explain`. [#60](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/60)

0.23.0: SimPy parity

- **SimPy parity:** every SimPy 4.1.2 feature natively in YAML, the builder and the low-level API, each checked against SimPy, such as nested conditions, event callbacks, unlimited stores and custom resource types. The SimPy Compatibility page lists each one, and the three differences kept by design. [#71](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/71)

0.22.0: Native core, experiments and replications

- **Native core parity:** the operations on the SimPy Compatibility page work natively in YAML, the builder and the low-level API, and each is checked against SimPy. They include signals, interrupts, tasks needing several resources, filtered store gets, stopping and stepping a run, and customers who give up on a queue or never join it. [#64](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/64)
- **Breakdowns, changing demand and replay:** a resource that fails and is repaired, a schedule of times at which an arrival rate or a capacity changes, and arrivals read from a local CSV or Parquet file. [#65](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/65)
- **Replications:** run a model with many seeds and get each statistic with a [95% interval](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/concepts/output-analysis/#interval-and-half-width), so a result is never read from one run. [#59](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/59)
- **Experiments:** compare designs and sweep parameters over [replications](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/concepts/output-analysis/#replications), fail an experiment when a result breaks a limit, fit a distribution to measured data, and write a Markdown report, all on one machine. [#66](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/66)
- **Speed:** faster runs that publish the same records. [#24](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/24)
- **Record contract:** every record field documented with its type and format, payload keys such as `__table__` reserved for desflow, a `timezone` setting for timestamps, and no `lag_seconds` from a run at full speed. [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)
- **Learn section:** the shop tutorial extends one shop model page by page and answers a question with a number on each page. It has 20 pages, and the new pages cover replications, comparing designs, sweeps, fitting, patience, interruptions, end conditions and more. [#60](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/60)

0.21.0: Distributions, flows and statistics

- **Distributions and seeds:** more distributions, including `empirical`, which draws from values measured in a real system. Each distribution draws from its own random stream, so adding an arrival leaves the other draws unchanged. desflow needs Python 3.11 or later. [#42](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/42)
- **Ingress messages:** every ingress connector, Kafka, Redis and PostgreSQL, takes a parameter change as `path` and `value`, the names a scenario step already uses. [#51](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/51)
- **Stores, containers and priority:** tasks take items from stores and amounts from containers, and a resource serves its queue oldest first, newest first or by task priority. [#43](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/43)
- **Flows:** routing between tasks by a condition or by probability, entity state that an order keeps from task to task, and delays without a resource. [#44](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/44)
- **Statistics and ground truth:** wait and service times, throughput, [utilisation](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/concepts/queueing-basics/#utilisation) and queue length as telemetry, with a [warm-up](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/learn/concepts/output-analysis/#one-run-starts-empty) period; and ground-truth records of what a scenario changed, so a detector or an agent can be scored against them. [#45](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/issues/45)

0.20.0: Rename to desflow

- **Rename to desflow:** the package, its import name and its command are all `desflow`. The old names, `dynamic-des`, `dynamic_des` and `ddes`, were removed in 1.0.

The [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/changelog/index.md) lists every release.

# Upgrading to 1.0

This page is for a model, a script or a pipeline that runs on desflow 0.28.0. Each item says what 0.28.0 did, what 1.0 does and what to change. 1.0 follows SimPy's rules for time, ties and failures, so a seeded model can publish other records than it did on 0.28.0, and some YAML forms now mean something else. From 1.0 the [Compatibility Policy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/compatibility/index.md) applies, and a 1.x release no longer changes a result without listing it.

To move a model to 1.0:

1. Install desflow 1.0 and uninstall `dynamic-des` if it is still installed, as [Removed Names](#removed-names) says.
1. Run `desflow check` on every blueprint. It names each key or value that 1.0 refuses, with its line.
1. Run the model's tests, such as `desflow test`, and compare its stored results. Where a test fails, find the change below that explains it. `desflow test --fix` writes the new values once you accept them.

## Removed Names

- **`dynamic_des` and `ddes`.** 0.28.0 kept the import name `dynamic_des` and the `ddes` command, each with a warning. 1.0 removes both: `import dynamic_des` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, and no `ddes` command is installed. Import `desflow` and run `desflow`. Uninstall `dynamic-des`; its last release installs a desflow below 1.0.
- **`**registry_kwargs` of `ConfluentAvroSerializer` and `ConfluentAvroDeserializer`.** 0.26.0 deprecated the confluent-kafka keys. 1.0 removes them, and a call that passes one raises `TypeError`. Pass the named argument instead: `basic.auth.user.info` (`user:password`) becomes `auth=("user", "password")`, `ssl.ca.location` becomes `verify=`, `ssl.certificate.location`, `ssl.key.location` and `ssl.key.password` become `cert=`, and `max.retries` becomes `max_retries=`. The `bearer.auth.*` keys with the source `STATIC_TOKEN` become `headers={"Authorization": "Bearer <token>", "target-sr-cluster": "<logical cluster>"}`, with `"Confluent-Identity-Pool-Id": "<pool>"` when `bearer.auth.identity.pool.id` was set. Delete `cache.capacity` and `cache.latest.ttl.sec`, which had no effect. [Connect to a Secured Schema Registry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/kafka-security/#connect-to-a-secured-schema-registry) shows the arguments.
- **`desflow.core.distributions`.** The module is gone. `DISTRIBUTIONS` is in `desflow.models.distributions` in 1.0, a module path that 1.x does not promise to keep. `desflow dist` lists the families from the command line.
- **Modules of `desflow.core` that declare and run a model.** `desflow.core.context`, `desflow.core.signals`, `desflow.core.task`, `desflow.core.flow`, `desflow.core.scenario`, `desflow.core.breakdowns` and `desflow.core.internal` are gone, and so is `desflow.blueprint.cli`, and importing one raises `ModuleNotFoundError`. Their code is in `desflow.builder` and `desflow.cli`, module paths that 1.x does not promise to keep. The 0.28.0 API Reference showed `SimulationContext`, `Signal`, `SignalFailed`, `TaskFailed`, `Router`, `Transfer`, `run_scenario` and `run_breakdowns` at these paths. Import each from `desflow`: an import of `SignalFailed` from `desflow.core.signals` becomes `from desflow import SignalFailed`. Their loggers moved too, as Logger names under [Builder and Low-level API](#builder-and-low-level-api) says.

## Run and Time

- **`strict` defaults to SimPy's rule.** In 0.28.0, `strict` was false in YAML and the Builder unless it was set, and it was never checked at `factor: 0`. In 1.0 it is true when it is not set and `factor` is above 0 or `go_live_at` is set, so a paced run that falls behind the wall clock raises `RuntimeError`. An explicit `strict: true` at `factor: 0` raises once the wall clock has moved, as SimPy does. `--sample`, replications, `desflow experiment` and `desflow explain --verify` run at `factor: 0` and ignore `strict`. Set `simulation.strict: false` (`SimulationContext(strict=False)`) to keep the old behaviour. See [Strict Pacing](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/clocks-and-pacing/#strict-pacing).
- **`on_unhandled_failure` defaults to `stop`.** In 0.28.0, YAML and the Builder defaulted to `continue`, so a failure that nobody handled ended one entity's flow and the run went on. In 1.0 the default is `stop`, as in SimPy and the Low-level API, and the run ends with the error. A model that relies on the old rule adds `run: {on_unhandled_failure: continue}` (`run(on_unhandled_failure="continue")`). See [Handle a Failure Nobody Handles](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/failures/#handle-a-failure-nobody-handles).
- **Signals fire once.** In 0.28.0 a signal re-armed after it fired. In 1.0 a signal fires once by default, as SimPy's `Event` does: a wait after the firing resumes at once, and a second firing is refused. Give a signal that fires more than once `once: false` (`add_signal(name, once=False)`, `Signal(env, name, once=False)`). A `once: true` signal that fired again dropped the second firing with a warning; it now raises under `on_unhandled_failure: stop`. See [One-Shot Signals](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#one-shot-signals).
- **A run with no `until` ends.** In 0.28.0 such a run never ended while statistics were on, or with a sink at a `factor` above 0, or with an ingress connector. In 1.0 it ends when only desflow's own events are left, and a `stop` that can no longer happen raises SimPy's `RuntimeError`. Give such a run an `until`. A live model meant to run on gives its connector an `until`. See [Stop Early](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#stop-early).
- **A Low-level run to an event ends.** In 0.28.0, `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment.run(until=<event>)` ran for ever on desflow's own timers when the event never came. In 1.0, with no ingress set up, it ends with SimPy's `RuntimeError` when no model event is left; with an ingress it goes on. Name a time as well: `env.run(until=event | env.timeout(t))`.
- **No smallest delay.** In 0.28.0 a service time or a drawn delay was at least 0.00001 seconds. In 1.0 the floor is 0: a constant 0 takes no time, and a normal draw below 0 is raised to 0. A constant gap of 0 starts entities at one instant without end, so the run never ends and `until` does not stop it, as in SimPy. Give such an arrival a gap above 0.
- **`sim_ts` is not rounded.** 0.28.0 rounded `sim_ts` to three decimals. 1.0 writes the clock as it is, so `1.357` may read `1.3565...`. Round `sim_ts` before you compare it. See [Field Values](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/#field-values).
- **A number keeps the type it is written in.** 0.28.0 converted times, amounts, container capacities and priorities to floats. In 1.0 a number keeps its written type: `env.now`, `peek()` and the readings of a step or segment print `5` for a time written `5`, where they printed `5.0`. A live update keeps the number as written, so `3` written over `2.5` is `3`. The record fields `capacity`, `level`, `wait_max` and `usage_since` are integers when their inputs are, such as `38` where 0.28.0 wrote `38.0`. `sim_ts` stays a float. Iceberg and Parquet sinks still write a statistic's `value` and `usage_since` as doubles. Text written over a parameter is still read as a float.

## Order at One Instant

These changes make a task go on in the same step as the SimPy process it stands for, so records at one instant can change order, and a unit or an item can go to another entity at a tie. A model with no events at the same time publishes the same records.

- **A task with one `wait` branch** now goes on in the step its event is processed, as `yield event` does in SimPy. To keep the old order, write the branch under `any`, as `wait: {any: {only: {timeout: 2}}}`. A `wait: {timeout: 5}` with `patience: 5 s` now starts and finishes at 5, where it reneged; the `any` form gives the old result.
- **`next`, `on_fail` and `on_interrupt_next`** now run the following task in the same process and the same step, so it asks for a unit before a child spawned at that instant, and a process you wait for ends when its whole flow ends. To let the child go first, give the following task `wait: {timeout: 0}`, which matches SimPy. A `subscribe` interrupt or a preempted kept unit now reaches the following task, which `on_interrupt: abandon` cuts short.
- **A task's `on:` actions** now run in the step the task ends, before its next task starts. A flag they set is read by the next task, but not by a `next` condition on the same task, which is chosen before they run. To run them one step later, fire a signal in the task's `on:` and put the actions in that signal's `on:`.
- **Tied replay rows** now start in one step, in file order, before any of them takes its first step. 0.28.0 started each row in a separate step.
- **An `interrupt` reaches an instance made in the same step,** from `spawn:` in `on:`, `context.spawn`, `context.call` or a `next` chain. In 0.28.0 it found no instance. The task keys `spawn:` and `interrupt:` still run interrupt first, so one task's own pair does not reach the new instance; two `on:` entries in the order spawn, interrupt do.
- **Patience at a tie.** When a patience ends at the instant a unit is granted and the patience's event comes first, the task now reneges. 0.28.0 served it. The same holds for a `get`, a `wait` branch and a request asked again after a preemption.
- **A grant at the end of a wait.** A request, get or put branch counts as won only when it was processed before the wait's condition, as `req in result` is in SimPy. An item a `get` was granted after that is lost. A request granted by then keeps its unit until the task ends. Order the events so the grant comes first when the model needs the unit or item.
- **Equal priorities in a priority store** now leave in the order SimPy's heap gives, which is not put order from four items on. To keep put order, give each item a priority that rises, such as `priority: "1 + process.instance / 1000000"`; in the Builder and the Low-level API a pair `(priority, number)` is a valid priority. See [Start With Items and Serve by Priority](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/stores-and-containers/#start-with-items-and-serve-by-priority).

## Resources, Waits and Interrupts

- **A unit is kept through a plain interrupt.** With `on_interrupt: resume` or `restart`, a plain interrupt no longer gives back a unit the task holds, so the task goes on with it, and other entities wait until the task ends. A task with several resources asks again only for the unit it lost. A unit kept with `keep` now goes back at once when the next task reneges, fails or has no next task. To give the unit back and queue again, use `on_interrupt: abandon` with `on_interrupt_next` naming a task that asks for it. See [Interrupts](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#interrupts).
- **A granted `request` branch under `restart`.** In 0.28.0, an interrupt of a task with `on_interrupt: restart` gave back every granted `request` branch of its wait and asked again at the back of the line. In 1.0 the task keeps them and starts the other branches again. To queue again as before, write the task with `on_interrupt: abandon` and `on_interrupt_next` naming a copy of it, and name both tasks in every `interrupt` that names the first.
- **Interrupt or preemption at the end of the work.** A job interrupted or preempted at the instant its work ends now ends at that instant, publishes no `resumed` and asks for no unit. In 0.28.0 it waited for a further 0 seconds.
- **`keep` and a child flow.** A child flow started by `wait: {task: ...}` no longer gives back the unit its parent kept when it starts, balks or is abandoned. The unit stays until the parent's next task starts. A model that counted on the early release ends the parent's task with no `keep`.
- **Opposite-order acquisition loads.** 0.28.0 refused a model whose tasks take shared resources in opposite orders. 1.0 loads it and logs a WARNING from the logger `desflow.builder.context`, and the run can stop if two tasks wait for each other. A test that expected the `ValueError` reads the warning instead.
- **Preempting a finished process.** A unit held by a process that has ended, such as a Low-level `request` never released, now fails the flow that preempts it with SimPy's `RuntimeError`. 0.28.0 took the unit with no error. Release a unit before its process ends, with `resource.release(request)` or a `with` block.
- **Builder `preempt` as text.** `task(preempt="f")` was kept as text and counted as true. In 1.0, `"f"`, `"no"`, `"off"` and `"0"` are false, as in YAML. Write `preempt=True` or `preempt=False`.
- **`queue_limit` is a registry path.** A resource now has the path `<sim>.resources.<r>.queue_limit`, and `DynamicResource.queue_limit` is a read-only property that follows it, so `resource.queue_limit = 5` raises `AttributeError`. Change it with `env.registry.update("<sim>.resources.<r>.queue_limit", 5)`. `compile_parameters()` gives a resource as a subclass of `CapacityConfig` that also holds the limit, so compare its `current_cap` and `max_cap` rather than the whole object. See [Queue Limit](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/units-and-queues/#queue-limit).
- **A `batch` with a `timeout` whose members all leave** before it closes is dropped, so the next member starts a new batch and its `timeout` and `batch.age` count from that member. Compare the stored results of a model whose batch members can renege, balk or be interrupted while they wait. See [Know What Happens to a Member](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/serve-entities-together/#know-what-happens-to-a-member).

## Failures

- **A task that ends in a run failure runs none of its `on:` actions,** as no statement runs after an uncaught exception in SimPy. That covers a `next` condition that cannot be evaluated, a wait that fails because its child did, and a function that raises, when no `on_fail` handles it. A task's own `fail` condition, and a failure that `on_fail` handles, keep their actions.
- **A failed evaluation in a task with `on_fail`.** A generator or a step that raises in a task with `on_fail` now goes to `on_fail`, where 0.28.0 stopped the run. Remove `on_fail` from the task when the run must stop.
- **A `fail` expression that cannot be evaluated,** such as `payload.a == 2` on a payload without `a`, now fails the task: it publishes `failed` with the error as its reason, and the run stops with `TaskFailed` under `stop` and goes on under `continue`. In 0.28.0 the error left the run with no `failed` record, even under `continue`.
- **A child flow that fails after its waiter was abandoned** no longer raises `TaskFailed` under `continue`; the run goes on. Under `stop` it is unchanged.
- **An empty or zero failure reason is kept.** A child flow's or a wait's failure with `fail_reason: ""` or 0 replaced the reason with the error's text, such as `signal 's' failed:`. In 1.0, `upstream.reason` reads the reason as given. Give the failing task a reason that is not empty, or read the empty reason in the handler.
- **`on_fail` without `fail`** is accepted in YAML and the Builder, and catches a task function that raises. Only `fail_reason` without `fail` is refused, as "fail_reason needs a fail condition".

## Values and Expressions

- **A mapping with a `gen` key is a generator.** In 0.28.0 such a mapping was data in `attributes`, store `items`, an interrupt `cause`, a `fire`, `on:` or timeout `value`, a `payload`, `set` and a scenario `value` and `record`. In 1.0 it is a generator, or a load error with the line. A key named `gen` directly under `set`, `attributes` or `record` is still a field name. To keep such a mapping as data, write `{gen: literal, value: {gen: 5}}`, which publishes `{"gen": 5}`. See [Generated Values](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#generated-values).
- **`item.<field>` where no `get` reaches** is refused at load, with the task named. In 0.28.0 it read nothing and failed when the run reached it.
- **A name that does not exist in `resume` or `open`.** A `lookup`, `aggregate` or `registry[...]` read that names a missing task, row or path in a `resume` or `open` value is refused at load. Correct the name.
- **Builder times.** `True` or `False` as a time, in `SimulationContext(initial_time=)`, `warmup`, `lag_interval`, a `drain` limit or a time-valued distribution parameter, was taken as 1 or 0 seconds. In 1.0 it raises `ValueError`, as a blueprint does. Write the number of seconds.
- **Builder draws in a `wait` or `open`.** A generator in a Builder `wait` or `open`, such as an `each` count or a timeout's `after`, now draws from the stream of its place in the blueprint, so the Builder gives the numbers of the same blueprint. At the same seed it gives other draws than 0.28.0. Compare the stored results of such a model again.
- **A sim id with a dot,** such as `Shop.v2`, draws the same random times as the same model with a plain sim id, so its results for a seed differ from 0.28.0. Record its results again.
- **An element named like a kind.** A live update of an element is stored by its kind alone. A resource named `service`, `containers` or `variables` has its capacity cast to a whole number, a container named `stores` keeps a fraction, and a whole-number variable named `max_cap` or `current_cap` refuses `inf`. The same holds for a sim id whose second part is a kind, such as `Shop.service`.

## Sinks and Connectors

- **A status record** (`queued`, `started` and each other status of a task) carries `sim_id` and `service` beside `path_id`. 0.28.0 wrote `path_id` alone. A consumer that checks the fields of a status value, or a table whose columns 0.28.0 records made, gets the two new fields. See [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md).
- **Routing keys in a payload.** A payload key `__topic__` (Kafka), `__table__` (Iceberg) or `__path__` (Parquet, JSON Lines) now chooses the destination, and the sink removes it. 0.28.0 dropped it with a warning. Rename such a key if it was only data. A `__table__` that PostgreSQL and Iceberg share on one record needs the form `namespace.table` for Iceberg, or a `table_router`. See [Reserved Payload Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/#reserved-payload-keys).
- **A sink with `upsert_keys`** now writes the other records of a batch and skips only those that have none of the key columns, with one warning per flush that gives the counts. 0.28.0 lost the whole batch. Check the warning count after a run.
- **An Iceberg column that is an integer in the first batch** is no longer truncated when a later batch holds a fraction: that batch is logged at ERROR and lost. Name the column as a double in `schemas`, such as `schemas: {shop.events: {key: string, v: double}}`. See [Iceberg](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#iceberg).
- **A statistic and a reading need separate destinations.** A statistic's `value` is a number and a reading's is a mapping, so a `table_router` or `path_router` that sends telemetry to Iceberg or Parquet gives readings a table or path of their own.
- **`KafkaIngress` creates its topic** at the start of a run when it is missing. Give `topic_policy: manual` to keep it from creating one.
- **A Kafka record its serializer refuses** is skipped with a warning that names its key and the reason, and the rest of the batch is sent. 0.28.0 stopped the batch and retried the connection.
- **A PostgreSQL sink with `envelope` on** warns when it skips a record whose value is not a mapping. The reason in that warning, for every sink, now reads "which this sink cannot write as a row".
- **Parquet, JSON Lines and Iceberg sinks** load their libraries before the run starts. In a strict paced run without `logical_start_time`, the records are stamped behind the wall clock by the load time. A run with `strict: false` keeps its 0.28.0 timestamps.
- **A Parquet, JSON Lines or Iceberg sink without its extra** is refused when it is built, with an `ImportError` that names the extra. 0.28.0 built it, and the run wrote nothing.
- **`ConsoleEgress()` with no logging at INFO,** such as `python FILE` with no `logging.basicConfig`, prints one `UserWarning`. The records are the same.
- **`KafkaAdminConnector.get_state()`** keys a sim id and a service id that hold a dot by their whole names, such as `Shop.v2`, where it took one part of each.

## Builder and Low-level API

- **A second `run()` of one context** starts from the model's starting values, as a new context does, not from the values the first run changed. Pass other starting values to `start()` as `overrides`, or read the values a run ended with from `context.env.registry` before the next run.
- **`compile_parameters()`** gives the config objects as the model declares them, so a capacity or a stream name left out is `None`. Read the starting values a run registers from `registry_paths()`.
- **A task function that replaces `context.sampler`, `context.values` or `context.sim_id`** during a run no longer changes the arrivals, breakdowns and family members of that run. Set them before `start()`.
- **After a `start()` that fails before it makes the run's holders,** `get_resource`, `get_store` and `get_container` raise `KeyError`, where they gave the previous run's object.
- **`egress_*` lists of `DynamicRealtimeEnvironment`** are read-only: assigning one raises `AttributeError`, and changing a list it returns does not reach the egress. Pass the sinks to `setup_egress`.
- **`fields` of `add_arrival_replay` and `read_trace`** takes `"all"` or a list of columns, as a blueprint's `replay.fields` does. Write `fields=["id"]` for one column. See [Replay](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/#replay).
- **A Builder `on=` entry,** in `task(on=)`, `task(listen=)` and `add_signal(on=)`, refuses a key other than the actions, `value` and `when`, where 0.28.0 ignored it. Remove the key, or move it into the action's own mapping.
- **An index on a number,** such as `users.machine[0]`, is refused when the Builder context starts (`run()` or `start()`), not at `task()`. A Low-level `Expression("users.machine[0]")` now parses.
- **`load_context(folder, "file.py", preview)`** applies the preview to the Builder file, where 0.28.0 raised `ValueError`.
- **Logger names.** The messages that `SimulationContext` and its signals log came from the loggers `desflow.core.context` and `desflow.core.signals` in 0.28.0. In 1.0 they come from `desflow.builder.context` and `desflow.builder.signals`. Set a level on the new names, or on `desflow`, which holds both. A filter applies only to the messages of the logger it is added to, so add it to each new name, or to the handler.

## Command Line and Installs

- **desflow needs pydantic 2.6.1 or later,** where it accepted 2.6.0.
- **`desflow check FILE.py`** imports a Builder file and prints `ok FILE (sim_id ID)`, or the error. 0.28.0 exited 1. A Low-level file is refused.
- **`desflow check`** exits 1 for a blueprint whose `tests` entry has no seed in a file with no `simulation.random_seed`, and, in a run with no end, warns about each arrival with no `max_events`. The exit code of that warning is still 0. See [desflow check](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/check/index.md).
- **`desflow run FILE.py --sample`** prints the Builder file's first events. Without `--sample`, or with `--stdout`, `--var` or `--watch`, it exits 2 as before.
- **`desflow fit`** writes its settings file in the blueprint layout: the comment wrapped at 88 characters, a blank line between keys and long lists wrapped. The file loads to the same settings.
- **`desflow fit` and `fit_column`** skip `poisson` and `geometric` named in `candidates`, as "counts whole numbers".
- **`desflow report` and `run_experiment`** build the report without reading `results.csv`, so a missing `results.csv` no longer stops the report.
- **An experiment's counts** are the task and flow counts that are 0 when no entity reached them; another whole-number statistic is no longer listed among them.

## Error Messages

A test that matches the text of an error matches the new text:

- The priority, patience and balk checks name `seize` and `open`: "needs a resource, a seize or a request in its wait or open".
- `on_balk` "needs a balk, a resource, a seize or an open", and the messages on `cause.<name>` and `upstream.<field>` also name `on_interrupt_run`, `on_renege`, `on_balk` and `on_fail`.
- An index on a number reads "'machine' is not a family; add family: true to its entry".
- `stats` with no `level`: "stats needs a level, unless it sets only trace, when the level is none".
- A `telemetry` entry with no `function`: "a telemetry entry takes exactly one of function and readings".
- An arrival: "an arrival takes exactly one of dist, replay or gap", and "an arrival with replay takes no distribution parameters".
- A task with a resource "needs a service or a service_time".
- A wait timeout: "a wait timeout is seconds, a duration such as '5 min' or an expression".
- The line of an error inside a wait is the line of the key, not of the `wait`.
- The warning of a sink that drops a reserved payload key names each routing key and its sink.
- A `Template` whose generator does not parse is refused when it is made, with the parse error.

# Compatibility Policy

From 1.0, a model, a script or a pipeline written for one 1.x release runs on every later 1.x release. A 1.x release may add a key, a command, an option, a name or a record field. It does not remove one, and it does not change what one means. Each promise below has a test that fails when a change breaks it, so a release cannot break a promise by mistake. [Upgrading to 1.0](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/upgrading-to-1.0/index.md) lists what changed from 0.28.0 to 1.0.

## What 1.x Keeps

| Promise                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | What a 1.x release may change                                                                                                        | Test that guards it                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The YAML blueprint format: every key, its type and what it means                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | add a key, a value or a form; widen a limit; make a required key optional. Every difference from the 1.0 schema must be one of these | `tests/unit/test_yaml_format_frozen.py`                                |
| The `desflow` command: every command, argument and option, and how a 1.0 command line is read                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | add a command, an option that is not required, or a choice; widen a limit. Every 1.0 command line parses to the same values          | `tests/unit/test_cli_surface.py`                                       |
| The public Python API: every name at the import paths listed below, with its signature, including the schema registry serializers and deserializers                                                                                                                                                                                             | add a name, or an argument with a default                                                                                            | `tests/unit/test_public_api.py` and `tests/unit/public_api.txt`        |
| The record format of [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md): each field with its name, type and position                                                                                                                                                                          | add a field after the last one of its kind, or a record kind that reaches only the sinks that ask for it, as `trace` does            | `tests/unit/test_record_contract.py`                                   |
| The extra names of `pip install "desflow[<extra>]"`: `kafka`, `redis`, `postgres`, `confluent`, `glue`, `parquet`, `iceberg`, `fit`, `watch`, `fake` and `all`                                                                                                                                                                                  | add an extra                                                                                                                         | `tests/unit/test_extras.py`                                            |
| The registry path forms, such as `<simulation>.resources.<name>.current_cap`, that an ingress message, a scenario step and `registry.update` write to                                                                                                                                                                                           | add a form                                                                                                                           | `tests/unit/test_registry_paths.py`                                    |
| The reserved payload keys: a key with two underscores on each side belongs to desflow, a sink drops the keys it does not route by, and `__topic__`, `__table__`, `__path__` and `__stream__` choose the destination, as [Reserved Payload Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/#reserved-payload-keys) says | add a key                                                                                                                            | `tests/unit/test_record_contract.py` and the routing test of each sink |

The public Python API is every name exported at these import paths:

- `desflow`
- `desflow.values`
- `desflow.blueprint`
- `desflow.analysis`
- `desflow.explain`
- `desflow.models`
- `desflow.resources`
- the connector modules under `desflow.connectors`, such as `desflow.connectors.egress.kafka` and `desflow.connectors.ingress.file`

The [API Reference](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/api/index.md) shows each name at its path. A name imported from a module inside a package, such as `desflow.builder.context` or `desflow.blueprint.build`, works in 1.0 and may stop working in a later 1.x release, so import it from the path the API Reference shows.

## What Is Not Covered

- **Seeded output.** The records of a seeded run can change between 1.x releases, such as when a fix changes a draw or the order of events at one instant. Such a change is never made without a note, as the next section says.
- **`desflow explain --json`.** Its shape can change in 1.x, and its `schema_version` changes with it.
- **A form marked experimental.** A key or a command added in 1.x while it is marked experimental can change until a release removes the mark.
- **A Python version.** A 1.x minor release may drop one, as [Supported Versions and Platforms](#supported-versions-and-platforms) says.
- **Simulation server.** The server, its MCP tools and its `pattern` blueprint block ship after 1.0 behind the `server` extra and start as experimental. Its REST API under `/api/v1` only adds once it is released.

## No Silent Change to Results

A change to the result of a valid blueprint is a break, even where seeded output is not promised. The release lists it under Upgrading in the [Changelog](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/changelog/index.md), with its reason. The `regression` job of the CI pipeline runs every example, conformance blueprint and regression scenario on the last release from PyPI and on each new commit, and fails on a difference that `tests/regression/expected.yaml` does not list with the release that made it. From 1.0 it also runs the files of `v1.0.0` on desflow 1.0.0 and on the new commit, so an edit to an example cannot hide a change in what a 1.0 blueprint does.

## Deprecation

A name, key or option that a 1.x release replaces keeps working with a `FutureWarning` for at least one minor release. The warning names its replacement. It is removed only in the next major version, 2.0, and the Upgrading section of that release says what to change.

## Breaks After 1.0

A break is made only in a major version. It needs a stated reason and an Upgrading line with the old behaviour, the new behaviour and what to change. Where it is cheap, the release also adds a setting that keeps the old rule for one major version.

## Supported Versions and Platforms

Fixes, including security fixes, ship in 1.x releases, and a release before 1.0 gets none. [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/desflow/blob/v1.0.0rc3/SECURITY.md) says how to report a vulnerability. 1.0 supports Python 3.11 to 3.15, the versions the CI pipeline tests. A 1.x minor release may drop a Python version that has reached its end of life, or that a dependency no longer supports. That is not a break: the release raises `requires-python`, so pip installs the last release that supports the older Python.

| Platform             | What is supported                                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Linux                | every feature, including the examples that run services with [odctl](https://github.com/jaehyeon-kim/odctl) |
| Windows through WSL2 | the same as Linux, and the recommended way to run desflow on Windows                                        |
| macOS                | the core library and the command                                                                            |
| Windows              | the core library and the command; the service stacks of the examples are not supported                      |

## Older Docs

The docs of each published release stay on the site under its version. A version other than the latest shows a banner that links to the latest. The docs of 0.20.0 to 0.28.0 show no banner, because each was built with the templates of its release, before the banner existed. Those releases came before this policy, so their pages promise no compatibility.

# Changelog

Each release, newest first: what changed, then under Upgrading what to change in code, commands or installs that use the previous release.

## Version 1.0.0

desflow 1.0 is the first stable release. From 1.0, the YAML blueprint format, the `desflow` command, the public Python API and the record format stay compatible across 1.x, as the [Compatibility Policy](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/compatibility/index.md) sets out. 1.0 also follows SimPy's rules for time, ties and failures, so results and some YAML forms change from 0.28.0, and [Upgrading to 1.0](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/upgrading-to-1.0/index.md) lists each change.

- A blueprint needs no Python for any of the known cases that the tests run in YAML, the Builder API and the low-level API, and SimPy's seven examples are written in desflow in [SimPy Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/examples/index.md). [SimPy Compatibility](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/simpy/compatibility/index.md) shows each SimPy construct in the three forms, with its status.
- `run.segments`, `run.steps` and `run.sync` stop a run at several points, publish a reading after each model event and re-anchor the wall clock, as stepping a SimPy environment does. See [Run in Segments](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/time-and-pacing/run-length/#run-in-segments).
- Generators, a mapping with a `gen` key, make each value of a record: random numbers, choices, Faker text, identifiers, times, sums, conditions and the model's state, and a task draws named values with `vars`, `vars_once`, `on_start` and `finish_vars`. See [Generators](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/generators/index.md) and [Generated Values](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#generated-values).
- `lookup`, `previous`, `upstream` and `aggregate` read the records that tasks published earlier, with `history` setting how many a task keeps. See [Read Earlier Records](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/task-flow/#read-earlier-records) and [Look Up Other Records](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/generate-data/look-up-other-records/index.md).
- An expression takes `**`, functions such as `abs`, `round`, `sqrt` and `log`, lists, mappings, comprehensions, `arg.`, `cause.` and `upstream.` names, and the state calls `held`, `waiting`, `putting`, `getting`, `peek()` and `running`. See [Names an Expression Reads](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/blueprints/#names-an-expression-reads).
- `poisson` and `geometric` join the distribution families. See [Distributions](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/distributions/index.md).
- An arrival takes `gap`, `first_at`, `max_events`, `count`, `keys`, `group`, `active`, `off_mode` and `initial`, and a task takes `service_time`, `key`, `payload: null`, `activate` and `deactivate`, so a source starts entities by a count, a key list or a computed gap. See [Start Entities](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/model-parts/arrivals-and-services/#start-entities).
- `seize` and `release` hold a unit across tasks, `open`, `cancel` and `{handle}` name a request or an event and cancel it, `whole_flow` waits for a flow, and a `queue` or `preempt` rule, `get_queue` and `put_queue` rank a line by an expression. `queue_limit` is a registry path. See [Hold a Unit Between Steps](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/several-resources/#hold-a-unit-between-steps), [Name an Event and Cancel It](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#name-an-event-and-cancel-it) and [Rank the Line by an Expression](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/priority-and-preemption/#rank-the-line-by-an-expression).
- `suspend` and `resume` park a task until another resumes it, `on_interrupt_run` runs a task when one is interrupted, `on_renege`, `on_balk` and `on_fail` alone send a flow on after it leaves the line or fails, and `upstream.status` and `upstream.reason` say why. See [Park a Task Until Another Resumes It](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#park-a-task-until-another-resumes-it) and [Leave the Line](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/tasks/#leave-the-line).
- `breakdown.clock: busy` counts the time to a failure only while a resource works. See [Count Only the Time the Station Works](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/breakdowns/#count-only-the-time-the-station-works).
- `batch` serves entities together. Tasks with one `batch.name` share a batch, and under `resume` and `restart` an interrupted member of an open batch leaves it and joins again at the back. See [Serve Entities Together](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/modelling/serve-entities-together/index.md).
- `stats.on_change` publishes the readings of a resource after each request and release, `stats.trace` with a `when: trace` sink publishes each model event, and `telemetry.readings` publishes readings of your own with no Python. See [Publish at Each Change](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#publish-at-each-change), [Trace the Events](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#trace-the-events) and [Add Readings of Your Own](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/results/statistics/#add-readings-of-your-own).
- `family: true` with `members` makes a family of resources, stores, containers or signals, and `{of, key}`, `{of, lowest}`, `wait: {each}`, `open` with `each` and `{handle, index}` pick and wait for its members. See [Make a Family of Resources](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/resources/units-and-queues/#make-a-family-of-resources) and [Pick a Member of a Family](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#pick-a-member-of-a-family).
- `fire.fail`, `fire.defused`, `signals.<name>.defused`, a computed `fail_reason`, `fire.priority`, `listen` and `when` on an `on:` entry fail, defuse and order events, and run actions on another task's event. See [Actions When an Event Happens](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/signals-and-waiting/#actions-when-an-event-happens) and [Failures](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/tasks-and-processes/failures/index.md).
- `desflow check` builds blueprints and Builder files without running them, warns about a run with no end, and refuses a test with no seed in a file with none. `desflow test` runs the `tests` of a blueprint, and `--fix` writes the new values. `--var NAME=VALUE` fills `${NAME}`, and `desflow run --watch`, with the `watch` extra, runs a file again after each change. `desflow run --sample` takes a Builder file. See [desflow check](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/check/index.md), [desflow test](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/cli/test/index.md) and [Write Tests in the Blueprint](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/analysis/test-a-model/#write-tests-in-the-blueprint).
- `envelope: false` writes each record's value alone, `topic_policy`, `topics` and `table_policy` create topics, tables and namespaces, `serializer` names a schema serializer in YAML, and `ssl` and `sasl_oauth_token_provider` connect to a secured Kafka. `__topic__`, `__table__` and `__path__` in a payload choose the destination, and a Kafka sink with `envelope: false` sends a null value as a tombstone. See [Write the Value Alone](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#write-the-value-alone) and [Reserved Payload Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/#reserved-payload-keys).
- A status record carries `sim_id` and `service` beside `path_id`, the two names `path_id` joins, so a reader no longer splits `path_id`. See [Records and Telemetry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/records-and-telemetry/index.md).
- The Builder and the low-level API have a form of every new key, and the Builder's `add_service`, `add_arrival` and `add_breakdown` read a duration such as `"4 min"`. See [Arguments for the Keys of a Blueprint](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/builder-api/#arguments-for-the-keys-of-a-blueprint) and [Low-level Forms of the Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/writing-a-model/low-level-api/#low-level-forms-of-the-keys).
- `ParquetStorageEgress`, `JsonlStorageEgress` and `IcebergStorageEgress` refuse to be built without their extra, with an `ImportError` that names it, and a `ConsoleEgress` in the `log` format warns when logging at INFO is off, because it would print nothing.
- 1.x keeps every YAML key and its type, every record field with its type and position, every extra, every registry path form, every reserved `__name__` payload key and the `desflow` command line, and tests fail on a removal. The import paths 1.x keeps are `desflow`, `desflow.values`, `desflow.blueprint`, `desflow.analysis`, `desflow.explain`, `desflow.models`, `desflow.resources` and the connector modules. `Preview`, `Candidate`, `render_terminal`, `QueueFull` and the new `check_model` are exported from them. See [API Reference](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/api/index.md).
- 1.0 removes the names that earlier releases deprecated: the `dynamic_des` import name, the `ddes` command and `**registry_kwargs` of `ConfluentAvroSerializer` and `ConfluentAvroDeserializer`.
- Fixes: a Kafka, Redis or PostgreSQL sink lost its last batch when a run ended quickly; a second `run()` of one context started from the values the first run changed; `desflow explain` missed the tasks started by `on:` and `listen` spawns, task branches, `on_interrupt_next` and `on_interrupt_run`; a count of 0 was read as missing by `replicate`, experiments, `desflow test` and `explain --verify`; the JSON Lines and console JSON sinks stopped after one batch they could not write; and an interrupt with `on_interrupt: resume` that came at the instant a task's patience ran out stopped the run with `ValueError: Negative delay`.
- The YAML files of the examples and the docs are written in one layout, and `desflow fit` writes its settings file in the same layout: the comment wrapped at 88 characters, a blank line between keys and long lists wrapped.
- The docs are rewritten for 1.0. The Gallery holds the end-to-end examples, How-To has a Generate Data group and guides for Records and Kafka, Storage and Tables, and Analysis and Tools, a new guide tests a pipeline against planted faults, and the Agent Skill section covers the desflow skill for AI assistants. The skill checks a model against its request, teaches how to test a model and port a SimPy program, and bundles `scripts/check_model.py`, which compares the records of the three forms. The docs of a version other than the latest show a banner that links to the latest.

### Upgrading

- 1.0 changes results and some YAML forms. [Upgrading to 1.0](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/about/upgrading-to-1.0/index.md) lists each change with the old behaviour, the new behaviour and what to change. The changes most models meet are the defaults of `strict` and `on_unhandled_failure`, signals that fire once, the end of a run with no `until`, an unrounded `sim_ts`, numbers that keep their written type, and tasks that go on in the same step as SimPy's process, which changes the order of records at one instant.
- The log messages of a model's declaration, checks and signals come from the loggers `desflow.builder.context` and `desflow.builder.signals`, which were `desflow.core.context` and `desflow.core.signals`. A level or a handler set on `desflow.core` no longer applies to them: set it on `desflow.builder` as well, or on `desflow`, which covers both.

## Version 0.28.0

- `SimulationRegistry.change` sets a value and returns a `ParamChange` that says what was stored, or raises `ParamRejected` when the registry refuses it. See [Know Whether a Change Was Refused](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#know-whether-a-change-was-refused).
- `on_change`, on the registry and on `SimulationContext`, is a list of callbacks that receive a `ParamChange` for every accepted change, with its source: an ingress connector and its class, a scenario step, or the overrides of `start()`. See [Follow Every Change](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#follow-every-change).
- `update`, `set_exactly` and `start()` take `source`, `actor` and `reason`, which each `ParamChange` carries.
- `SimulationContext.registry_paths()` returns the paths and starting values of a run without running it. See [Find the Path](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#find-the-path).
- `FileIngress`, `type: File` in YAML, changes parameters during a run when you edit a local YAML file, with no service. See [File](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/ingress/#file) and the [File Steering example](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/ingress/#example-file-steering).
- The AI skill and [Draft a Model](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/ai/draft-a-model/index.md) teach how to draft a model from a description of a process.

### Upgrading

- A scenario step whose value the registry refuses, such as an exponential rate of 0, now stops the load of a blueprint with its line, and `start()` of a builder model. `start()` checks the scenario with its overrides, so an override or an experiment design that makes a later step's value invalid also stops the start. A run stops with `ParamRejected` at a step's time when an ingress message, an `on:` action or a process has made the step's value invalid, and a low-level `run_scenario` raises it for any refused value. Before 0.28.0 the value was logged and ignored, and the run went on. Values sent by ingress connectors and `on:` actions are still logged and ignored. See [Stability and Limits](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/live-parameters/#stability-and-limits).

## Version 0.27.0

- `GlueAvroSerializer` and `GlueAvroDeserializer` talk to AWS Glue with desflow's own client and wire format, so the `glue` extra no longer depends on aws-glue-schema-registry. The arguments and the bytes on the topic are the same.
- The `kafka` extra no longer installs kafka-python. `KafkaAdminConnector.create_topics` and the topic creation of `KafkaEgress` use aiokafka.
- JSON Schema and Protobuf are read and written through both schema registries, next to Avro, by `ConfluentJsonSchemaSerializer`, `ConfluentJsonSchemaDeserializer`, `ConfluentProtobufSerializer`, `ConfluentProtobufDeserializer`, `GlueJsonSchemaSerializer`, `GlueJsonSchemaDeserializer`, `GlueProtobufSerializer` and `GlueProtobufDeserializer`. See [JSON Schema](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/json-schema-and-protobuf/#describe-the-record-in-json-schema) and [Protobuf](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/json-schema-and-protobuf/#describe-the-record-in-protobuf).
- The builder and low-level scripts of the [Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis and Related Records examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/index.md) stop at `EXAMPLE_UNTIL` simulation seconds when that variable is set, and run until Ctrl + C when it is not.
- A new How-To group, Storage and Tables, has two pages: [Write to Cloud Storage](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/storage-and-tables/cloud-storage/index.md) writes Parquet and JSON Lines files to S3, Google Cloud Storage or Azure Blob Storage, and [Write to Iceberg Tables](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/storage-and-tables/iceberg-tables/index.md) appends to a table through a SQLite, REST, PostgreSQL or Glue catalog. Each has YAML, Builder and Low-level forms.

### Upgrading

- The `glue` extra no longer installs `aws-glue-schema-registry`. Code that imports `aws_schema_registry` itself must add it to its own dependencies.
- Glue schema registration waits up to 30 seconds (10 checks, 3 seconds apart) for a new schema version to become available. aws-glue-schema-registry 1.1.3 waited 3 seconds once and then checked 10 times with no wait between checks.
- Glue registry and framing failures raise desflow's `SchemaRegistryError` and `SerializationError`, importable from `desflow.connectors.egress.kafka` and `desflow.connectors.ingress.kafka`, not `aws_schema_registry.SchemaRegistryException`.
- `GlueAvroDeserializer` compiles a JSON schema version with fastjsonschema, as aws-glue-schema-registry 1.1.3 did, and the `glue` extra needs fastjsonschema 2.22.1 or later, where 1.1.3 accepted any 2.x release from 2.15. A JSON schema version that fastjsonschema cannot compile, or a record that is not JSON, does not match the schema or cannot be checked against it, raises `SerializationError`, where 1.1.3 raised the exception of fastjsonschema, orjson or Python, or its own `ValidationError`.
- The `confluent` extra also installs `jsonschema` and `protobuf`, and the `glue` extra also installs `protobuf`.
- The `kafka` extra no longer installs kafka-python. `KafkaAdminConnector` takes aiokafka's admin settings, so a kafka-python-only setting such as `ssl_cafile` is refused: pass `ssl_context`. A kafka-python token provider is refused too: pass `KafkaAdminConnector` the aiokafka provider that `KafkaEgress` takes, as [AWS MSK (IAM)](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/kafka-security/#connect-to-aws-msk) shows. Code that imports `kafka` itself installs kafka-python separately. `KafkaAdminConnector.create_topics` raises the `aiokafka.errors` class for a broker error, such as `aiokafka.errors.InvalidReplicationFactorError`, where it raised the `kafka.errors` class: catch `aiokafka.errors.KafkaError` instead.

## Version 0.26.0

- The `confluent` extra no longer installs confluent-kafka. desflow writes and reads the Confluent Schema Registry wire format itself with httpx and fastavro, so the extra no longer depends on a package without Python 3.15 support. The bytes on the topic are the same.
- `ConfluentAvroSerializer` and `ConfluentAvroDeserializer` take named arguments for a secured registry: `auth`, `verify`, `cert`, `timeout`, `headers`, `proxy` and `max_retries`. See [Connect to a Secured Schema Registry](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/how-to/records-and-kafka/kafka-security/#connect-to-a-secured-schema-registry).
- A Parquet or JSON Lines egress writes to Google Cloud Storage and Azure Blob Storage, from a `filesystem` mapping with `type: gcs` or `type: azure`, in YAML, the builder and the low-level API. See [Parquet and JSON Lines](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#parquet-and-json-lines).
- An Iceberg egress writes through a SQL catalog on SQLite or PostgreSQL and through a Glue catalog, and the `iceberg` extra installs what they need. See [Iceberg](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/user-guide/live-runs-and-connectors/egress/#iceberg).
- Python 3.15 is supported. On 3.15 the `kafka`, `confluent` and `glue` extras build aiokafka, and the `iceberg` extra builds pyiceberg and zstandard, from source, which needs a C compiler. See [Installation](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/installation/#install-the-package).
- `GlueAvroSerializer` serializes a record. It failed on every record in every release since 0.7.0.
- The docs are reorganised. Learn holds the tutorial and, after it, the concept pages, each explained from the tutorial's shop. Command Line and SimPy and desflow are sections of their own. The examples are the [Runnable Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/index.md) group of How-To, and its overview page holds [Services for the Examples](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/gallery/#services-for-the-examples), the odctl profiles each example needs, which moved from Installation.
- Model code is shown in YAML, Builder and Low-level tabs on every page except those about one way of writing, such as Builder API. Every How-To script has all three forms, each with a test, except on the two pages about blueprints alone, Call Python from YAML and Set Up Your Editor.
- The Cheat Sheet and YAML Format pages are removed. [YAML Keys](https://jaehyeon.me/desflow/latest/reference/yaml-keys/index.md) is the one list of blueprint keys, and both old addresses lead to it.
- Each page's address follows the sidebar, such as `cli/run/` for `desflow run` and `how-to/modelling/breakdowns/` for Model Breakdowns. Every old address, and every old link to a moved section, leads to the new place.

### Upgrading
